My Illinois vs. UCLA prediction sees Bret Bielema's Illini as a live underdog, and my full college football picks predict defense to rule the day. FOX covers this contest at 9 pm ET on Friday, Nov. 13. TOP PICK Who will win Illinois vs UCLA: Illinois +9.5 Sell high on UCLA and take Illinois at +8.5 or better. The Bruins are 9-0 ATS and are running away with the Big Ten, but that doesn't mean they're a juggernaut. No single result on their resume is something Bret Bielema's squad isn't also capable of pulling off, so these teams are therefore still in a similar tier. UCLA's offense has stalled, ranking 86th in success rate and 133rd in explosiveness since Week 6 . That concern is exacerbated after starting tackle Hall Schmidt and starting center Riley Robell left the Minnesota game with injuries. Illinois has the better offense, checking in at 39th in EPA per play and 33rd in explosiveness over that span, and is therefore an appealing two-score underdog. Illinois vs UCLA Over/Under pick: Under 48.5 In a wet, rainy, short-week game, I'm betting on sloppy offensive results. Illinois' defense has experienced a revival since coordinator Bobby Hauck was fired. The secondary is a strength, featuring a wealth of experience, and a green front seven has drastically improved since the start of the season. Neither team will push the tempo, leading to a leisurely pace and offenses that rely on sustained drives. The Bruins rank 125th in seconds per snap (29.2), preferring to slowly drain the life out of opponents, and the Illini aren't far ahead at 90th (27.4). 2026 Week 11 Preview: Wake Forest Demon Deacons @ SMU Mustangs
picks.blurb: 2026 Week 11 Preview: Wake Forest Demon Deacons @ SMU Mustangs | Underdog Dynasty Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo A Rest of the FBS Community Underdog Dynasty November 13, 2026 Underdog Dynasty Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Conference USA Sun Belt Conference American Athletic Conference Betting FanDuel College Football Odds College Football Picks and Predictions Community Guidelines Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Conference USA Betting Expand FanDuel College Football Odds All communities Notifications ACC Wake Forest is rolling toward the ACC title game. But SMU, which has never lost a home ACC game, can stay in the race. Time and date: Saturday, November 14 at 12:00 p.m. ET Network: ESPN Location: Gerald J. Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-1.5) Over/under: 61.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 3-1 Last meeting: Wake Forest 13, SMU 12 — October 25, 2025 Current streak: Wake Forest, 1 (2025) Setting the scene This might be the ACC regular season game of the year. For the first time in College Football Playoff history, the ACC champion is guaranteed an automatic bid. Thus, just getting access to Charlotte keeps the door ajar for Wake Forest and SMU in this high-stakes conference showdown. The Demon Deacons are one of the hottest teams in college football, winning six consecutive games, primarily in blowout fashion. But the Mustangs haven’t ever lost an matchup at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, faring 12-0 in their previous contests. A Wake Forest win propels the Demon Deacons to the doorstep of the ACC Championship Game. An SMU win creates chaos, bringing a cluster of 2-loss teams back into championship consideration, including itself. The ACC races greatly hinges on what unfolds Saturday afternoon on The Hilltop. Wake Forest Demon Deacons outlook Wake Forest (8-1, 5-1 ACC) is ranked No. 13 by the College Football Playoff committee, situated as the second-highest ACC team. Since its lone September loss to Miami (FL), the Demon Deacons have been as dominant as anyone in the FBS. During the last five games of its six-game win streak, Wake Forest has defeated opponents by an aggregate score of 264-31, or an average of 53-6 per game. The Demon Deacons used a dominant defense to stun SMU 13-12 in last year’s meeting in Winston-Salem, but this season, the offense has hit its stride under second-year coordinator Rob Ezell. Wake Forest ranks fourth nationally in scoring (43.3 points per game), ninth in total offense, and 10th in passing. Starting quarterback Gio Lopez missed last week’s game against FCS Merrimack with a lower body injury, but the absence was permissible due to the level of opponent. The former South Alabama and North Carolina gunslinger has been phenomenal in his new home, delivering 18 touchdowns against one interception this year, ranking 13th nationally in passing average. His mobility has made defenses pay too, accumulating 317 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the season. Lopez’s top target Carlos Hernandez is receiving national recognition. The senior is sixth in the FBS with an average of 105 receiving yards per game, and he regularly strikes from distance. Hernandez has multiple 70-yard touchdowns this season, and he has four outings with at least 110 yards and an end zone appearance. Jack Foley, Kam Shanks, and Antonio Meeks have provided support in this dynamic aerial attack, and the diversity in options allows Wake Forest to have the nation’s ninth-most efficient third down offense. The run game has been serviceable, ranking 43rd nationally in yards per game, while producing 4.94 yards per carry. Ty Clark and Deuce Lawrence have split carries throughout the season, totaling 416 and 327 rushing yards, respectively. Wake Forest’s offensive improvement has somewhat obscured the consistent impact of its defense. The Demon Deacons have only surrendered multiple scores once in their past five games, and they’ve finished 22 consecutive quarters without allowing more than seven points. The result is the country’s 13th-ranked scoring defense and 24th-ranked total defense — a unit which is particularly stingent against the run, surrendering just 85 yards per game on a 2.69 average. Defensive end Langston Hardy is the leader of the run-stuffing effort. He leads all ACC players with 13.5 tackles for loss, while also producing 44 tackles and 5.5 sacks. Backfield pressure has been a signature of this Wake Forest defense, and two other defensive linemen — Gabe Kirschke and Zach Lohavichan — have at least 7.5 tackles for loss. Wake Forest’s defense found the sustainable method of success, and that’s getting stops. The Demon Deacons are fifth nationally in both red zone defense and fourth down defense, finding ways to get off the field in critical situations. The unit can become even more dangerous if it dabbles in the turnover game. Wake Forest has forced just seven takeaways all season, which is tied for the eighth-fewest in the FBS. SMU Mustangs outlook SMU (7-2, 5-2 ACC) prepares for a revenge game against Wake Forest. Had the Mustangs prevailed last October in Winston-Salem, they would have competed in the ACC Championship Game with a College Football Playoff spot on the line. Instead, they fell in a 13-12 heartbreaker on a last-second field goal — one of the program’s four ACC losses since joining the conference in 2024. Zero of those losses transpired at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. SMU has been a different beast at home, and that was evident in its most complete game of the season last Friday against Virginia Tech. Counting games against FBS opponents, the Mustangs registered a season-high 23 first half points, utilizing its strongest start of the season to push past the Hokies, 51-28. The concept of senior day might have lost some luster in the transfer portal era, but Saturday will feature one of the most emotional senior day moments in recent memory. Kevin Jennings is in his fifth year with the program and third as the starting quarterback, and the Dallas area native has poured a lot into the program. Jennings guided the Mustangs to an American Conference title, an ACC Championship Game appearance, a College Football Playoff berth, and a Holiday Bowl victory. Now he’ll play his final game in Dallas, entering the pivotal matchup fifth nationally with 2,764 passing yards and fourth with 25 touchdown passes. The most remarkable part of Jennings’ eye-popping stats is his efficiency. For a quarterback that slings it deep quite often, the senior boasts a 73.9 completion rate, which is second among all players with at least 100 attempts. Jennings has also limited interceptions this year, finishing four of his last five starts without one. SMU’s high-powered passing attack involves a slew of receivers. Yamir Knight, coming off a 103-yard, 3-touchdown performance, is the most frequented with a team-high 50 catches. But Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale are also heavily involved — especially on downfield attempts — and all three average over 15.0 yards per reception this season. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrström are also regular targets, tied for second on the team with four touchdown receptions apiece. The Mustangs’ run game is statistically a middle-of-the-road unit, ranked 70th in yards per game and 66th in rushing average. Kendrick Raphael operates as the top option, and he’s scored in seven of nine contests this year. Freshman Christian Rhodes has seen an increasing number of reps since mid-October, and he’s coming off a career-high 92 rushing yards against Virginia Tech. On defense, SMU displays a similar identity to the previous Mustang defenses of the Rhett Lashlee era: defensive line dominance. The Mustangs are one of 17 programs racking up at least 3.0 sacks per game, and defensive end Marques White is the ringleader of the movement. The eighth-year senior notched his third multi-sack game of the season last week, contributing to the turnover battle with a forced fumble and fumble recovery on the same play. But unlike the previous two seasons, SMU isn’t collecting turnovers on a consistent basis. The Mustangs have forced just eight turnovers all year, recovering five fumbles and picking off two passes. Despite the lack of takeaways, the secondary has shown considerable improvement from 2025, skyrocketing from 135th to 42nd in passing yards allowed per game, with safeties Jimmy Wyrick and Sael Reyes playing significant roles in that progress. Last year’s matchup between SMU and Wake Forest was the ultimate defensive battle. Just two touchdowns were scored — one on a 14-play drive and another capping a 41-yard series. There were eight combined turnovers in the matchup, which was decided on Connor Calvert’s 50-yard field goal as time expired. This year’s rematch looks bound to lean more on the higher-scoring end. Wake Forest brings significantly more offensive firepower in this matchup, headlined by the strong connection between Gio Lopez and Carlos Hernandez. The Demon Deacons’ offense has been virtually unstoppable since the start of October, and while SMU should provide some resistance with a formidable defensive line, Wake Forest will still get its points in Dallas. However, SMU can thrive in a shootout style game. The Mustangs are one of the most explosive offenses in the country, ranking ninth in the FBS with 15 plays spanning 40 yards. Wake Forest has excelled at preventing the big play this year, but the Mustangs’ receiving corps should present challenges on the back end that the Demon Deacons haven’t seen since the Miami (FL) loss. This back-and-forth thriller will come down to crunch time. With the backing of its home crowd, SMU improves to 13-0 in ACC matchups at Gerald J. Ford Stadium — a result which will add significant chaos to the final two weeks of ACC play. Game Info, Stats and Previews The Wake Forest Demon Deacons and the SMU Mustangs meet Saturday in college football action from Gerald J Ford Stadium in University Park. Here’s a collection of relevant information and reasoning for a sound SMU vs Wake Forest prediction. Wake Forest Demon Deacons Betting Preview The Demon Deacons have been playing quite well all season. They’ve only got one blemish on the card so far, a 33-20 los to Miami on September 18. Outside of that Wake Forest has beaten Akron, Purdue, Louisville, Stanford, NC State, California, Virginia and Merrimack this season. Across nine games thus far that gives the Demon Deacons a very nice 8-1 record in the books for their troubles. In their latest action back on Saturday versus Merrimack, Wake Forest didn’t have any troubles. picks.headline: Trenches Preview: Tennessee at Texas A&M
picks.blurb: Trenches Preview: Tennessee at Texas A&M - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Trenches Preview: Tennessee at Texas A&M COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: T.J. Searcy #18 of the Texas A&M Aggies reacts in the second half against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jay Arnold · SB Nation Wed, November 11, 2026 at 10:06 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Texas A&M returns to Kyle Field for the first time in three weeks after two straight road losses, sandwiched by an idle week. The Aggies fell 17-9 to South Carolina last time out in a contest that saw Texas A&M accumulate over 450 yards of offense and fail to produce a touchdown. The Aggies will hope to rectify that this week in College Station as they welcome the #8 Tennessee Volunteers to town. The trenches are going to be extremely important if Texas A&M is going to steal a win this Saturday. Let's dive into what needs to happen up front for the Aggies to come out on top. Offensive Line COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: Marcel Reed #10 of the Texas A&M Aggies runs with the ball in the first half against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images Against South Carolina, Texas A&M moved the ball well. As mentioned above, the Aggies racked up over 450 yards of offense. Rueben Owens ripped off multiple explosive runs, and Texas A&M had 206 yards on the ground. Yet, zero touchdowns made the hope that would be rendered by the yardage a grand disappointment instead. Simply put, field goals do not win games. The Aggies have to be able to finish drives off to win games, and Texas A&M has failed to do so in three out of the four road contests this season. The Texas A&M offense has fared better at home for the most part, but frankly I don't expect that to continue against an absolutely elite Tennessee defense. The Vols rank second only to Georgia in scoring defense. Tennessee's passing defense is staunch, though the Aggies wouldn't likely be able to test them there either. The rushing defense isn't in the upper tier of the conference but is also solid. Most significantly, the Volunteers lead the country in sacks. Defensive end Tyree Weathersby has seven sacks this season. The Vols also get pressure from the interior, as defensive tackle Xavier Gilliam has six sacks. Gilliam is a force to be reckoned with in the run game as well. I've thoroughly enjoyed watching film on the gifted DT this year, but I don't think his ability bodes well for this Texas A&M offensive line. I don't think this offensive line is horrible, and I think they've continued to play better as the season has progressed, but against this defensive front for Tennessee, it's going to feel like all that progress has left. In short, if the Aggies score a touchdown this week, I'd be surprised if it came from the offense. Defensive Line COLUMBIA, SOUTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 07: Marco Jones #10 of the Texas A&M Aggies plays against the South Carolina Gamecocks during their game at Williams-Brice Stadium on November 07, 2026 in Columbia, South Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the situation for the offensive side of the ball is dire, I think the defensive side of the ball largely shouldered the burden well against South Carolina. The Aggies held what was the top rushing offense in the country at the time to under 100 yards right up until LaNorris Sellers ripped off a big run at the end. The Aggies also sacked Sellers twice, including a massive strip sack by Bryce Perry-Wright. We'll see if those run game improvements carry over as the Aggies face yet another powerful rushing attack. Powered by the legs of running back DeSean Bishop, Tennessee is the current top rushing attack in the SEC. However, if Texas A&M can find a way to slow down this rushing attack, the Aggies just might have a chance in this one. Discipline and sure tackling are going to be of the utmost importance as this Josh Heupel offense looks to spread opposing defenses out in order to capitalize on seams. Missed tackles against this Tennessee offense are extremely disastrous, and the Aggies can't afford to lose one-on-ones. The front four must maintain gap discipline as the secondary will be forced to honor Tennessee's formations. Get Tennessee behind the chains, and this becomes a drastically different ball game. While Tennessee ranks at the top of the conference in rushing, the Volunteers are the only team in the SEC below Texas A&M in passing offense. After Faizon Brandon started the season under center for Tennessee, George MacIntyre has since taken over. However, neither QB is a game changer on this offense, making the Vols basically one-dimensional. The equation for success against Tennessee is simple. Stop running backs DeSean Bishop and Daune Morris or get ground to a pulp. If the Aggies can make the improvements against the run permanent, they can hang around in this one – and that starts with the defensive tackle position and Brandon Davis-Swain, DJ Hicks, CJ Mims, and Landon Rink, in my opinion. While I think the Aggies keep this contest close in the first half, I think repeated three-and-outs by the Aggie offense eventually allow the Volunteers to wear down the Texas A&M defense in the second half. I have Tennessee winning this one 20-3. #BTHOtennessee

Published: Nov 12, 2026 · 10:00 AM EST The Tennessee Volunteers have come up with 2 of the most impressive wins of the season in the FBS, a 26-10 point pounding of Alabama and last weekend's 34-6 drubbing of Kentucky . Both teams were in the top 6 of the initial College Football Playoff Rankings. But despite the Vols being 7-2 with those 2 victories, and despite Tennessee's 2 losses each coming by a field goal against teams currently in the top 20 of those rankings, the Vols probably have to win out to make the field of 12. The Fearless Prediction knows how difficult it can be to win on the road in the SEC but will readily accept the challenge to make the correct call in Saturday's Tennessee- Texas A&M game. This will only be the second time that the Vols have made a trip to College Station. Back in 2016, they lost at Texas A&M in double overtime, 45-38, in a game best remembered for Tennessee RB Alvin Kamara's dominating performance. He had 18 carries for 127 yards and 2 TDs to go with 8 catches for 161 yards and a TD. It was the only game in Kamara's 2 seasons in Knoxville in which he was the focal point of the UT offense. If that doesn't summarize the missed opportunities of the Butch Jones era, nothing will. Fast forwarding to today, Tennessee's offense might not have a Kamara, but it does have a Bishop. The Vols' senior RB, DeSean Bishop, already has 1,066 rushing yards this season, and now stands 426 yards away from breaking Dylan Sampson's single-season rushing record of 1,491 rushing yards. Bishop (and Tennessee's offensive line) gets better as the game continues, and that certainly helps the cause with youth at QB. Redshirt freshman George MacIntyre completed 9-of-14 passes for 125 yards against UK, but more importantly he didn't throw an interception and he didn't fumble. But Josh Heupel added a wrinkle to the QB position, with true freshman Faizon Brandon (remember him?) seeing his first action since being pulled in the Auburn game a month ago. Brandon only took a couple of snaps. One in a single wing formation that resulted in a 29-yard run, and one a beautifully designed play in which Brandon tossed the football approximately 5 centimeters forward to Mike Matthews for what counts as a 24-yard TD pass. Heupel has now given opposing defensive coordinators more reason for concern the rest of the season, not knowing what else Heupel will come up with that Brandon package. Defensively, Tennessee continues to impress. It kept Kentucky out of the end zone for 60 minutes. It sacked UK QB Kenny Minchey 4 times while forcing 3 turnovers against a team that rarely coughed up the football. Tennessee is tied for 10th nationally in scoring defense (allowing 15.1 points per game), 18th in total defense (296.4 yards per game), and leads the nation in sacks with 39. LB Arion Carter is tops on the Vols in tackles with 59. DT Xavier Gilliam has a team-best 11.5 tackles for loss. As for Texas A&M, a season that began with so much promise has devolved into depression. The Aggies have lost 5 of their last 7 games, including a 17-9 defeat at South Carolina last weekend. They are 1-5 in SEC play. Mike Elko , now in his 3rd year as Texas A&M's head coach, has stuck with QB Marcel Reed, despite middling results. Reed throws for 182.3 yards per game, but his TD-to-INT ratio of 8:8 is not ideal. Rueben Owens II and K.J. Edwards combine to average 96.2 rushing yards per game. Mario Craver and Isaiah Horton are Reed's best options in the passing game, combining for 62 catches, 703 yards and 6 scores this season. Overall, the Aggies are only ranked 91st in the FBS in total offense, with 359.2 yards per game. The Aggies' defense will be a challenge for the Vols. ETSU and Tulsa transfer LB Ray Coney leads the team with 46 tackles. As a unit, they allow 320 yards per game, good enough to be ranked 28th nationally, while allowing only 18.7 points per game, 22nd in the FBS. Next week the Vols welcome Lane Kiffin and LSU back to Neyland Stadium. The Fearless Prediction will have a lot to say about that soon, but we aren't looking ahead. Tennessee better not either. And it won't. Kyle Field might be a tough place to play… but a lot of teams do win there. You'll be able to add Tennessee to that list. Fearless Prediction: Tennessee 24, Texas A&M 13 Mark Nagi has covered Tennessee athletics for over 20 years. He is the author of “Decade of Dysfunction,” an in-depth look at all that led to the crazy coaching search of 2017 at Tennessee. The book is available on Amazon. Tennessee is currently No. 8 in the College Football Playoff rankings. If they win out, they'll make the playoff and almost certainly host a game in the first round. But if they lose, they're probably out of the playoff. So, yeah, it's a must-win game for Tennessee this weekend (the Vols lost in their only previous trip to College Station in 2016). ESPN's Greg McElroy makes his score prediction for Tennessee vs Texas A&M ESPN's Greg McElroy, who has been quite accurate with his predictions for Tennessee this season, made his final score prediction for the matchup between the Vols and the Aggies. McElroy thinks the game will be close, but he ultimately has Tennessee pulling out a 23-21 win at Kyle Field. “Tennessee runs the ball better, but A&M does get off the field on third and long better than almost anybody,” said McElroy. “That could keep the game a little bit shorter. And short games could be decided by kickers, and field goals still matter. That's why this one sneaks over the number (the over/under is 43.5). “ I like Tennessee to win the game 23 to A&M's 21 , which means A&M is going to keep it really close. But in a close game, I just trust Tennessee more than I do the Aggies right now. picks.blurb: Tennessee vs. Texas A&M final score predictions: Can the Vols keep their playoff hopes alive in a tough environment? Skip to content NFL Close Menu All NFL Buffalo Bills Miami Dolphins New England Patriots New York Jets Baltimore Ravens Cincinnati Bengals Cleveland Browns Pittsburgh Steelers Houston Texans Indianapolis Colts Jacksonville Jaguars Tennessee Titans Denver Broncos Kansas City Chiefs Las Vegas Raiders Los Angeles Chargers Dallas Cowboys New York Giants Philadelphia Eagles Washington Commanders Chicago Bears Detroit Lions Green Bay Packers Minnesota Vikings Atlanta Falcons Carolina Panthers New Orleans Saints Tampa Bay Buccaneers Arizona Cardinals Los Angeles Rams San Francisco 49ers Seattle Seahawks College Football Close Menu All College Football Alabama Crimson Tide Auburn Tigers Florida Gators Georgia Bulldogs Miami Hurricanes Michigan Wolverines Notre Dame Fighting Irish Ohio State Buckeyes Oklahoma Sooners Ole Miss Rebels Penn State Nittany Lions Tennessee Volunteers Texas A&M Aggies Texas Longhorns Draft Simulator Trade Simulator CFB Playoff Predictor NFL Playoff Predictor Toggle Mobile Navigation Home The Vols take to the road against an A&M team that is reeling but talented. The Tennessee Vols head to College Station this weekend for a showdown with the Texas A&M Aggies. Despite being 4-5, A&M isn't playing terrible football, competing with both Alabama and South Carolina in recent weeks on the road. Tennessee comes in at No. 8 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings, and they control their own path to almost certainly a home playoff game if they can take care of business. Will they start on the right foot at Kyle Field on Saturday? Our college football writers weighed in with their predictions. Tennessee 23, Texas A&M 16 This has been a game that, from an upset perspective, is more of a concern to me than the Kentucky game was. Tennessee is a different animal on the road in SEC play than they are at home under Josh Heupel. Pre-snap mistakes and head-scratching moments seem to happen more away from home, and despite Texas A&M being 4-5, Kyle Field will likely still be loud and rocking on Saturday. I still think Tennessee is in good position to win here based on their line play on both sides of the ball, although the loss of Tyree Weathersby stings. But Tennessee's ground game and physical defense proves to be enough to get out of town with a tough win and set up a de facto playoff game for them against LSU next week. Craig Smith , A to Z Sports Tennessee Tennessee 27, Texas A&M 10 This Tennessee defense is playing lights-out. One of the best in the country. And after putting up 450 yards of total offense last week, A&M still managed just nine total points vs. South Carolina. Their offense has been bad, and the defense hasn't been great, either. Tennessee will use this game to find a bit of a spark in the passing game and continue running the ball well. Justin Churchill , A to Z Sports Oklahoma Tennessee 30, Texas A&M 17 There are no down weeks in the SEC, even if Texas A&M is having a down year. For the Vols, this is a bit of a trap game. The Aggies are not what many predicted based on preseason rankings, and the matchup with LSU next week could very well be for a CFP spot when all is said and done. But it won't matter if Tennessee doesn't take care of business this week. The Vols have the two things that travel and make a good football team however: a run game and good trench play. I expect Tennessee to overpower the Aggies and get out with a victory ahead of a monumental matchup next week. Rob Gregson , A to Z Sports Alabama Tennessee 31, Texas A&M 14 Tennessee has its top-10 spot and will cruise into the College Football Playoff if it can avoid another loss. Texas A&M has been reeling badly, losing three of its last four games, and will fall to 4-6 following Week 11. The Vols are going to get the job done on the road, avoiding a potential upset ahead of a big game against LSU next weekend. This Tennessee defense is bad news for the Aggies’ offense, and it could be a long day as a result. Brandon Little , A to Z Sports Ohio State Tennessee 28, Texas A&M 17 I expect Tennessee to have a tougher time early than some might anticipate. The Vols could come out a little sluggish offensively, allowing Texas A&M to hang around and potentially control portions of the first half. However, Tennessee has enough talent and offensive firepower to eventually find its rhythm. I like the Vols to make some adjustments at halftime, get the running game going, and put more pressure on the Aggies defense as the game progresses. The biggest difference comes down to quarterback play. Marcel Reed continues to have issues taking care of the football, and those mistakes are particularly costly against a Tennessee team that can turn turnovers into points quickly. The Aggies make a few plays to stay competitive, but they give Tennessee too many extra opportunities. The Vols take control in the second half, pull away late, and come away with an important SEC victory. Ryan Roberts , A to Z Sports Notre Dame Tennessee 27, Texas A&M 13 This has a chance to be really ugly. The Volunteers are in a good spot inside the top-10 of the College Football Playoff rankings with a fantastic run game. The only thing that will keep the Aggies in the game is their run defense and Marcel Reed scrambling BS. I don't think the Volunteers defense will let him gash them. Things feel like they are spiraling for the Aggies, and this will further that. away.headline: Tennessee vs. Texas A&M initial availability report
away.blurb: Wednesday night, the SEC released the initial availability report. Weathersby joins six players already out for the season. Texas A&M lists offensive lineman Trovon Baugh as doubtful and wide receiver Mario Craver as questionable. Craver is the Aggies’ second-leading receiver with 311 yards and three touchdowns. Below is the full availability report for Texas A&M. Saturday, No. 8 Tennessee will take on Texas A&M on the road in College Station, Texas. The Vols are coming off their big win over the Kentucky Wildcats last Saturday. In that game, edge rusher Tyree Weathersby went down with a season-ending knee injury. Tennessee had stayed fairly healthy for a while after the first few weeks of the season. Weathersby was having an amazing season as the sacks leader on the team and third in the Southeastern Conference with seven. Weathersby also had 20 tackles, two fumble recoveries and even a pass deflection this season. “I hate it for Tyree,” head coach Josh Heupel said Monday. “He’s played extremely well. He’s worked extremely hard. He was playing his best football. And I know he’ll bounce back from it, but obviously a huge bump in the road for him.” During Saturday’s win, tight end DaSaahn Brame exited the game after failing to maintain control of a pass in the end zone, according to the officials. Brame’s head hit the ground hard, and he was eventually helped off the field. He is not on the report, and Heupel said on Monday’s “Mike Keith Show” that he should be good to go. Heupel also spoke to the incomplete call. “DaSaahn’s doing good. We feel like he’ll be in a great spot for game day. When I was talking with the officials, we hadn’t gotten the report back postgame yet. That typically happens in the middle of the week. “But at the end of the day, he didn’t come down with the football, didn’t maintain control of it when he was on the ground. So that was the ruling that they gave me, and they said that they did review it up top as well.” No. 8 Tennessee and Texas A&M will kick off at 3 p.m. ET Saturday at Kyle Field in College Station, Texas. The game will be televised on ESPN. The Vols will try for their first win at Kyle Field after losing in double-overtime, 45-38, during their only other visit there back in 2016. home.headline: South Carolina football’s LaNorris Sellers gets positive injury update after limping through Texas A&M game
home.blurb: With the South Carolina football team getting the win over the Texas A M Aggies on Saturday, 17-9, it featured a concerning injury outlook for quarterback LaNorris Sellers. As Sellers was limping throughout the South Carolina football win over the Aggies after a play in the second quarter, head coach Shane Beamer had an injury update that is sure to lift a weight off any fan’s shoulders. Sellers suffered an ankle injury in the second quarter of the aforementioned win for the Gamecocks as Sellers was sandwiched between two defenders, as he landed awkwardly along with the defenders on the ground, causing a fumble. Leaving the game, Sellers would come back for the start of the second half and finish the game, recording 251 passing yards and a touchdown throw with 34 rushing yards and a score. Speaking to the media on Sunday, Beamer said that “everything looks good” with Sellers the day after the win and that the concern level is “very low,” as the expectation is that he plays next Saturday against Arkansas, according to Jack Veltri. “Shane Beamer updates LaNorris Sellers: Everything looks good with him today. He felt good last night at 9:30. He felt good this morning. Tests were done this morning. Looked good,” Veltri wrote on X, formerly Twitter. “Concern level is ‘very low.’ Fully expects him to play at Arkansas.” That is no doubt great news for Sellers and the Gamecocks, as so far this season, the junior has thrown for 2,100 yards with 17 touchdowns and seven interceptions, plus 637 yards on the ground with seven scores. At any rate, Sellers and the South Carolina football program look to extend the winning streak to five games against Arkansas on Saturday. Like ClutchPoints’ content? Be sure to follow us. But the Hoosiers, who have yet to announce a starting quarterback for the game, can calm the waters by notching a quality win over the visiting Trojans. USC is lagging outside the CFP picture…for now. That will change if the Trojans can upset IU on the road after beating Ohio State in their last game during Week 9. A win would also catapult USC into the Big Ten title race, revitalizing a season that appeared to be in peril after a 24-7 loss at Wisconsin on Oct. 24. The question is which Indiana quarterback the Trojans will be tasked with defending. Season-long starter Josh Hoover injured his throwing arm during Indiana's Week 9 win over Minnesota and was benched after subsequent struggles. Veteran backup Grant Wilson entered and completed 9 of 17 passes for 156 yards and a touchdown, sparking a quarterback controversy. Hoosiers coach Curt Cignetti was noncommittal this week on who will take the first snaps for IU, forcing USC to be ready for either option. The situation has created some late-season intrigue for the reigning national champions, who have been unable to pull away from most of their Big Ten opponents during an 8-1 (5-1 Big Ten) start. USC vs. Indiana: Need to know Can USC match Indiana's physicality?: Regardless of who is at quarterback for Indiana, USC's defense will have its hands full with the Hoosiers' skill talent. Physical receivers Charlie Becker and Nick Marsh comprise one of the best 1-2 tandems in college football. Meanwhile, IU running backs Turbo Richard and Lee Beebe Jr . are both averaging more than five yards per carry and are over 700 yards each for the season. USC has never been known for its physicality under coach Lincoln Riley, but keeping the Hoosiers in check will require it. Going on the road and winning against a team with Indiana's gritty DNA wouldn't just be a huge boost for the Trojans' playoff aspirations; it would also help change the perception of Riley's program. Indiana's CFP outlook: Indiana's chances of making the playoff will reach near "lock" status at 96.2% with a win, according to the CBS Sports CFP Forecaster. A loss would leave the Hoosiers with a 66.8% chance of selection and bring greater scrutiny to a resume lacking high-end fare. An Oct. 10 win over Nebraska is not aging well, as the Cornhuskers are on a four-game losing streak. After that, IU's best win is either on the road against a 5-4 Michigan team or at home against a 6-3 Northwestern team. However you slice it, the Hoosiers don't have a win against a team currently ranked in the CFP Top 25. Beating USC would change that...assuming the Trojans remain in the rankings. USC's CFP outlook: This is do-or-die for USC's playoff hopes. The Trojans' chances of making the field will rise to 51.5% with a win and plummet to 3.7% with a loss. In other words, the playoff has already started for Lincoln Riley's team. It's really a simple formula: finish 3-0 with wins over Indiana, Maryland and USC, and the Trojans will unquestionably make the playoff for the first time. Lose any of those games, and it's probably over for what is arguably the most historic program to have never appeared in the CFP. USC vs Indiana Prediction: Are the Trojans Really In the CFP Hunt?

Pete Fiutak · College Football News Thu, November 12, 2026 at 4:37 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Just when it seemed like USC was finished, and a new era would soon start with Lincoln Riley all but gone after an ugly 24-7 loss at Wisconsin, a funny thing happened – the Trojans rolled Ohio State 30-18. And now, at 7-2, with high-profile dates remaining against CFP No. 9 Indiana and No. 8 UCLA, No. 18 USC all but controls its own path to the CFP – a 10-2 Trojan team with two top-ten wins in the final three games wouldn't be a lock to get in, but … yeah, it would be. But Indiana is still pretty good. It's 8-1, this close to being 9-0, and even though the schedule hasn't been a killer, if it keeps winning, all will be just fine. But lose this, and the pressure will be on to avoid a slip over the last two weeks. USC vs Indiana: Quick Hits Indiana travels to Washington after this before finishing with the rivalry date against Purdue. USC hosts Maryland after this before the showdown at UCLA. It's just the fifth meeting ever, and the first since USC joined the Big Ten. The Trojans are 4-0, including the 1968 Rose Bowl. How To Watch USC vs Indiana Date: Saturday, November 14, 2026 Game Time: 3:30 PM ET TV: CBS Location: Memorial Stadium, Bloomington, IN – Week 11 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – How many 3-loss CFP teams will there be? Why USC Will Win Plenty of things have to go right. USC has the punting to own the field position game, there can't be a slew of turnovers, and Indiana has to keep struggling. The only way to put it is that it's like the Hoosiers forgot how to score. The offense is moving a bit, but it hasn't scored more than 20 points in regulation since early October. The USC passing game continues to be good enough. The ground game might be hit-or-miss, but Jayden Maiava is a smart, tough veteran who keeps hitting his throws for the Big Ten's best offense on third downs. Why Indiana Will Win Indiana got a week off to reset at just the right time. No, it's not playing nearly as well offensively as it did last year. No, it doesn't have that dominant mode, and it certainly doesn't have the same passing game. And yet it's still 8-1 – this bunch finds ways to win. For all of the issues on offense, the defense continues to be outstanding. The run D is the fourth-best in the nation, allowing just 2.3 yards per carry overall with no touchdowns in the last three games. USC might throw well, but it wasn't all that long ago that the ground game was stuffed for -18 yards by Wisconsin. USC vs Indiana Prediction, Betting Lines Is Grant Wilson up to the gig, or will Josh Hoover get the nod as he fights through an injury? No matter who ends up under center, he'll be fine against a USC defense that's been hit hard by injuries. Indiana's offense – even without banged up star RB Turbo Richard – will be a bit more effective than it was against Ohio State, Michigan, or Minnesota, but it'll be the defensive front and run defense that keeps the good season going. picks.headline: Former Notre Dame head coach picks USC to beat Indiana
picks.blurb: Former Notre Dame head coach picks USC to beat Indiana - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Former Notre Dame head coach picks USC to beat Indiana Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads As USC football prepares for a season-defining game at Indiana , one very interesting plot twist has emerged: A former Notre Dame head coach picked the Trojans to beat Curt Cignetti and the Hoosiers. Brian Kelly, now a commentator for CBS Sports, knows what it's like to coach in the state of Indiana. He recently said on air that Lincoln Riley's Trojans will go into Bloomington and win. This is not an earth-shaking story which possesses overwhelming significance, but it's a story worth noting because it's so fascinating on multiple levels. Brian Kelly had the upper hand over and against USC in most of the years he coached Notre Dame. Why is he trusting USC now? Notre Dame and Indiana fans had a very spirited argument before and after the Fighting Irish 's victory over the Hoosiers in the 2024 College Football Playoff. Notre Dame finished as the 2024 runner-up. 2025 Indiana, under Curt Cignetti, went one step beyond the Irish and won the national championship. Brian Kelly has no real reason to pick games for any reason other than he sincerely thinks one team will beat the other, but it's notable that he would trust USC and distrust Indiana. Both schools' fan bases don't like Notre Dame. It is simply interesting to wonder why Kelly is pivoting to the Trojans and away from the Hoosiers. Is there any underlying emotional reality which might have nudged Kelly in the direction of USC? Let's keep in mind that Kelly wants to return to coaching. Is his USC pick in any way motivated by how he sees the coaching carousel or the national landscape? We'll never know the answers, but the questions are legitimately interesting. home.headline: Indiana football gets good news on the injury report for quarterback Josh Hoover
home.blurb: BLOOMINGTON — Barring a setback, Indiana football quarterback Josh Hoover looks like he will be available to start against USC. The No. 9 Hoosiers (8-1, 5-1 Big Ten) do have some other injury concerns going into a must-win game against the No. 18 Trojans (7-2, 4-2). They have four key contributors (three starters) on the report with leading rusher Turbo Richard and defensive end Kellan Wyatt already listed as out for Saturday's game. Indiana has been down at least one running back — Khobie Martin missed half the season with an arm injury — for much of the year. Martin made his return to the lineup against the Gophers, but he only has three carries for seven yards on the season. The Hoosiers also listed cornerback A.J. Harris and linebacker Rolijah Hardy as questionable. Hardy was a late scratch against Minnesota with a back injury while Harris hobbled off the field in the second half. Harris missed time earlier this season with a knee injury, but played well after regaining his spot in the starting lineup. Jaylen Bell, who stepped in for Harris earlier this season, would likely get the start if the Penn State transfer is ruled out. Hoover, who suffered an upper body injury against Ohio State, wasn't listed on the initial availability report for the week that the Big Ten released on Wednesday night. Indiana coach Curt Cignetti declined to name a starter for this weekend's game against the Trojans , but Hoover will be in uniform as long as he remains off the report. Before the off week, backup quarterback Grant Wilson orchestrated a 23-16 comeback win in overtime against Minnesota after replacing Hoover to start the second half. Start the day smarter. Through nine games, the Boston College transfer leads the team with 745 rushing yards (6.5 yards per carry) and six rushing touchdowns. First-year freshman Jacob Savage started and played well in place of Hardy against Minnesota. His playing time had gone up in recent weeks with him landing in the rotation whenever IU went to a 4-3 defense. Against the Gophers, Savage had two quarterback pressures and four stops (plays that constitute a failure for the offense) while playing a career-high 60 snaps. (Photo by Gregory Shamus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Scotty White · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 1:00 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Michigan Wolverines suffered one of the worst losses in modern program history on Saturday, falling at home to the Michigan State Spartans, who came into the game sitting at 2-6 and on a six-game losing streak, 15-6. I've floated the phrase "rock bottom" around a couple of times this year, but this is it. We've hit rock bottom, and now the Wolverines have to go on the road to take on the Oregon Ducks. Last week, I predicted Michigan was going to lose to Michigan State because I didn't think that Kyle Whittingham was going to get his team motivated for a rivalry game. The Spartans are a bad football team, but they clearly have a coach who is trying and who cares. Sure enough, both teams embodied their head coach in that game. Michigan was lifeless, unenthusiasic, and just flat out looked like a team that didn't want to be there. After the game, Michigan fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck, which needed to be done. However, nothing will change until the Wolverines find a new head coach who embraces the program and actually wants to do his job. With a road test against a ranked team looming, things are only going to get worse. Here are a few predictions for this weekend's contest against the Ducks: Michigan will get shut out We almost saw this happen last week at home against one of the worst teams in the Big Ten, so why should we expect a better performance out west against the Ducks? Players have checked out and the head coach doesn't want to be here. The recipe going into this game could not be worse. Before the Michigan State game, things were bad, but a win would've made the Wolverines 6-3. And the losses, while painful and self-inflicted, were somewhat forgivable. However, there is no coming back from the atrocity we witnessed last weekend. It will only get worse. Kyle Whittingham will be fired after the game The one positive that will come from last week's disaster is that I can't see any scenario where Whittingham is Michigan's head coach on Dec. 1. The fan base is now completely against him, and the program is at its lowest point in over a decade. It's going to happen within the next month, and I think Saturday might be so bad that the school decides to get it over with before the end of the season. Oregon wins 17-0 I think that the defense will once again do enough to put Michigan in a spot to win a football game, but the offense isn't going to get it done. It will be another frustrating watch, but we will move one step closer to putting this dumpster fire of a season in the rearview mirror.

picks.headline: Michigan vs. Oregon Score Prediction: Wolverines Face Daunting Challenge At Autzen Stadium
picks.blurb: Michigan vs. Oregon Score Prediction: Wolverines Face Daunting Challenge At Autzen Stadium - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) Brandon Brown · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 13, 2026 at 7:07 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Michigan's 2026 season has been anything but predictable, but Saturday's trip to Eugene might present the Wolverines with their most difficult challenge yet. At 5-4 and coming off an embarrassing 15-6 loss to Michigan State, Michigan desperately needs something positive. Unfortunately, that opportunity comes against No. 18 Oregon inside Autzen Stadium, one of the loudest and most intimidating venues in college football. The Ducks will have the benefit of a hostile home crowd, while Michigan will be breaking in a new offensive coordinator and attempting to find some semblance of consistency on that side of the ball. It's hardly an ideal combination. When Michigan Has The Ball All eyes will be on interim offensive coordinator Jim Harding , who takes over following Kyle Whittingham's decision to fire Jason Beck. Michigan enters the matchup ranked No. 126 nationally in scoring offense, No. 109 in rushing offense, No. 125 in passing offense and No. 132 in total offense. Those numbers are remarkably poor for a program with Michigan's resources and expectations. Whittingham hasn't officially named freshman Tommy Carr the starter, but all signs point to No. 14 manning the offense. Carr has shown flashes since replacing Bryce Underwood, but he's also operating behind an offensive line that has struggled throughout the season. Against Oregon, those protection issues could become even more glaring. The Wolverines need Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter to establish something on the ground, particularly early. Otherwise, Carr could find himself facing obvious passing situations against an aggressive defense with the Autzen crowd making communication difficult. Harding doesn't need to reinvent the offense overnight. He needs to simplify things, establish manageable situations and give Carr opportunities to succeed. When Oregon Has The Ball Michigan's defense has been the more reliable unit by a mile, and that group will need another outstanding performance to keep this competitive. Defensive coordinator Jay Hill has enough talent to make things difficult, particularly with players like John Henry Daley, Zeke Berry, Chris Bracy and Jyaire Hill capable of creating disruptive plays. But Oregon presents a different challenge. The Ducks can put considerable pressure on a defense through tempo, athleticism, pure speed and offensive versatility. Michigan cannot afford repeated three-and-outs that force its defense to spend the afternoon on the field. If Oregon establishes an early lead, the Wolverines could find themselves in serious trouble. Michigan's defense should compete, but expecting Harding to completely transform one of America's worst offenses in less than a week is unrealistic. Autzen Stadium only makes matters worse. Offensive line coach Jim Harding will take over play-calling duties for an offense that ranks No. 126 nationally in scoring, No. 109 in rushing, No. 125 in passing and No. 132 in total offense. Expectations are understandably low, but perhaps a change in leadership will produce some unexpected results. 1. Michigan rushes for more than 175 yards With Harding now calling the plays, expect Michigan to double down on its physical identity. The longtime offensive line coach understands the strengths and weaknesses of his personnel better than anyone, which should lead to a more cohesive rushing attack. Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter will benefit from a simplified offensive approach, helping Michigan eclipse 175 rushing yards against the Ducks. 2. Tommy Carr plays turnover-free football Making another road start in one of college football's most hostile environments won't be easy for the freshman quarterback. However, Harding should make a concerted effort to put Carr in manageable situations rather than asking him to carry the offense. Carr will play a relatively clean game, make smart decisions with the football and avoid throwing an interception or losing a fumble. 3. John Henry Daley records two sacks Michigan's defense will need to create havoc to give the Wolverines a legitimate chance at pulling off the upset. Daley is arguably Michigan's most disruptive defensive player and has the ability to single-handedly derail possessions. Look for defensive coordinator Jay Hill to get creative with his pressure packages, allowing Daley to get after the quarterback and finish with two sacks. 4. Michigan scores a touchdown on its opening possession Considering Michigan didn't score a touchdown against Michigan State until the final moments, predicting an opening-drive touchdown against Oregon qualifies as extremely bold. Michigan takes Oregon into the fourth quarter within one possession There aren't many reasons to believe Michigan can beat Oregon on the road, but the Wolverines still have a defense capable of keeping them competitive. With an improved rushing attack, fewer offensive mistakes and some timely defensive stops, Michigan will shorten the game and frustrate the Ducks. Oregon will ultimately have more offensive firepower, but the Wolverines will make things considerably more interesting than most expect. Michigan will look noticeably better offensively under Harding, but the combination of Oregon's talent and the difficult road environment will ultimately prove too much. The Wolverines will show signs of life but remain one win short of bowl eligibility.

home.headline: Oregon's Teitum Tuioti exits Ohio State game with injury. What we know
home.blurb: Coach Dan Lanning said Nov. 9 Tuioti will be out for the rest of the season. The 6-foot-3, 263-pound senior out of Sheldon High School is the Ducks' third-leading tackler this season with 44. He also has a team-high 9.0 TFLs and eight quarterback hits. His 5.5 sacks are second on the team. Tuioti's injury came on a fourth-and-13 pass rush with 9:16 to play as his leg buckled when he was attempting to spin out of a block. COLUMBUS, Ohio – Oregon pulled off the upset Nov. 7 with a 41-28 win against Ohio State. But the victory came with a costly injury for the Ducks . Starting outside linebacker Teitum Tuioti injured his knee in the fourth quarter and was wearing a wrap as he was carted to the locker room after the game ended. "Unfortunately, Teitum's done for the year," Lanning said. "He had a knee injury, he'll end up having surgery. He's going to have to wait a little bit for things to settle down. I hate it for him, because it's kind of a routine, weird play that it happened on." In 51 career games, Tuioti has 200 tackles, 36.5 TFLs and 22.5 sacks. He was a three-year starter who does have one more season of eligibility remaining at Oregon, though a he also projected to be a Day 2 NFL Draft pick. "I don't know if he'll get another chance to play as an Oregon football player, but whoever gets to have that guy on their team in the future is going to be really really lucky," Lanning said. "Teitum has been unbelievable for us this year and every year that he's been here. Watching him grow as a player and as a person has been really fun for us." Teitum Tuioti injury: How it happened He was down on the field for a few minutes and needed help getting to the sideline. Tuioti had two tackles in the game, including one for a loss of yards. He also played a key role in one of the Ducks' most impactful plays when he took a direct snap with Oregon in punt formation and threw a 30-yard pass to fellow outside linebacker Matayo Uiagalelei for a first down. Chris Hansen covers University of Oregon football, men’s basketball, track and field, cross country and softball for The Register-Guard. You can reach him at chansen@registerguard.com .

picks.headline: 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line
picks.blurb: 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Sam Hutchens, Mississippi Clarion Ledger · The Clarion Ledger Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:03 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads OXFORD − Ole Miss football must win on the road against Oklahoma to keep hopes of a College Football Playoff appearance alive. No. 17 Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) will play at Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3) on Nov. 14 (3:15 p.m., SEC Network). The Rebels are coming off a 42-7 home loss to No. 1 Georgia that put its CFP hopes on the edge of extinction. A viable path to the CFP begins with winning the final three games of the season. This is the third consecutive season Ole Miss has faced Oklahoma and the Rebels have won the first two matchups. Like Ole Miss, the Sooners made the College Football Playoff in 2025. OU returned quarterback John Mateer but has struggled to complement a strong defense with a steady offense. Although the Sooners have losses to Michigan, No. 1 Georgia, No. 13 Kentucky and No. 24 South Carolina, OU has beaten two teams that Ole Miss lost to in No. 8 Texas and Florida. Here are five predictions about the matchup, including the final score: Jason Witten will have new wrinkles for OU offense vs Ole Miss defense The matchup pits defensive coaches against each other in Ole Miss' Pete Golding and OU's Brent Venables. Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten could be the wild card. The former Dallas Cowboys tight end was elevated to the interim offensive coordinator position after Oklahoma fired Ben Arbuckle. Five days after Arbuckle was dismissed, OU beat Florida 23-7 in a game where it had 351 total yards. The Oklahoma offense played clean, efficient football under Witten. The Sooners suddenly seem to have new life offensively, which comes at a bad time for an Ole Miss defense that was ravaged for 481 yards vs Georgia. Trinidad Chambliss, John Mateer both throw interceptions With three games remaining, Chambliss' interceptions have tripled this season. He threw three in a spectacular 2025 season, but is up to nine in 2026. Golding attributed the increase to a combination of bad reads, bad luck and bad throws. Chambliss has thrown at least one interception in seven games this season. That plays into the hands of Oklahoma, which is No. 4 in the SEC with nine interceptions. The Sooners are also No. 5 in the conference with 26 sacks. Chambliss has been more vulnerable when under pressure. OU quarterback John Mateer has had turnover problems as well. He's thrown seven interceptions and has two lost fumbles. Look for both defenses to come up with an interception. The Sooners' stingy defense is better prepared to recover from interceptions than Ole Miss. When OU picks off Chambliss, it will give the ball back to a Sooners' offense that looks well prepared to chew clock and limit the chances for the Rebels' offense. Ole Miss gives Makhi Frazier, Shekai Mills-Knight both at least 10 carries Even with a quarterback as capable as Chambliss, it will be hard for Ole Miss to attack Oklahoma through the air. OU has the No. 1 passing defense in the SEC (170.7 yards per game). OU is No. 7 in the SEC in rushing defense (122.6 yards per game), but it's the weaker of two stout options. Ole Miss needs running backs Shekai Mills-Knight and Makhi Frazier to play well. Those two players are the primary backs with Kewan Lacy ruled out with a shoulder injury. Mills-Knight and Frazier combined for 17 carries for 60 yards vs Georgia, but they should get more carries against Oklahoma. Oklahoma leads in time of possession, Ole Miss relies on big plays Opponents are 31-for-112 (27.7%) on third down conversions against the Sooners. That's the lowest mark in the SEC and No. 4 nationally. That indicates Ole Miss will have trouble maintaining long, slow-developing drives. The key to combat that is explosive plays. Ole Miss could use a big game from Deuce Alexander. The receiver leads Ole Miss with 669 receiving yards, but he was held without a catch against Georgia. He is Ole Miss' fastest, most explosive player and the primary threat to score a deep touchdown. Ole Miss is on the other end of the spectrum. The Rebels allow 44% of third down conversions, which is No. 14 in the SEC. The Sooners clinched the game against Florida with a 20-play march in the fourth quarter that consumed 12:45 on the clock. The Rebels must avoid that fate. Ole Miss vs Oklahoma score prediction Oklahoma 24, Ole Miss 23: This should be a close game that will be determined by whether Ole Miss' defense or Oklahoma's offense does better. Right now it feels like the OU offense has more momentum. The Rebels are more desperate, but feeling like you need to press and make big plays on the road against OU's defense is a bad place to be. X-Factor: Trinidad Chambliss Chambliss is my X-Factor because he will be coming off another tough game for him this season. He cannot let what rattled him last week take over. Bold Prediction: Ole Miss wins the turnover battle John Mateer has struggled to take care of the ball this year, and I believe Ole Miss will take advantage of that this weekend to give them the edge. Jacob Quaglino Score Prediction: Ole Miss 27, Oklahoma 24 X Factor Player: Trinidad Chambliss A theme this season, so far, seems to be that the entire team plays as well as its QB plays. On days when Chambliss is off a bit, the team as a whole typically doesn't play well, seemingly indicating that Chambliss may well be the X factor player in just about every game moving forward. Playing on the road has been a struggle for this team as a whole. The Ole Miss Rebels are 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play after their brutal 42-7 loss to Georgia last weekend in Oxford. Two weeks before that, they fell 34-27 at Texas. Those are two ranked opponents who are firmly in the College Football Playoff Conversation, but it's too late in the season to be dropping games like that. Now they head into a crucial SEC clash at Oklahoma on Saturday, with the CFP potentially hanging in the balance. More news : Brian Kelly Sends Blunt Warning to Texas Ahead of LSU Clash Lacy quickly emerged as one of the best players in college football last season, rushing for 1,567 yards (third most in FBS) and 24 touchdowns (second) on an FBS-leading 306 attempts, averaging 5.1 yards per carry, along with 177 receiving yards. He earned first-team All-American and first-team All-SEC honors, and entered this year on the preseason watchlist for several national awards. But Lacy injured his left shoulder in the Rebels' loss to Texas on Oct. 24, and hasn't been able to recover. His third, and potentially final, college season ends after just six games, finishing with 388 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns on 78 carries (5.0 yards per carry). Makhi Frazier, a Junior transfer from Michigan State, and sophomore Shekai Mills-Knight will continue to handle the bulk of the carries for Ole Miss. Frazier has 365 rushing yards on 72 carries this season (5.1 yards per carry), while Mills-Knight has 165 yards and three touchdowns on 33 carries (5.0 yards per carry). The Ole Miss Rebels are 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play after their brutal 42-7 loss to Georgia last weekend in Oxford. Two weeks before that, they fell 34-27 at Texas. Those are two ranked opponents who are firmly in the College Football Playoff Conversation, but it's too late in the season to be dropping games like that. Now they head into a crucial SEC clash at Oklahoma on Saturday, with the CFP potentially hanging in the balance. He earned first-team All-American and first-team All-SEC honors, and entered this year on the preseason watchlist for several national awards. But Lacy injured his left shoulder in the Rebels' loss to Texas on Oct. 24, and hasn't been able to recover. Star defensive back Peyton Bowen was a game-time decision last week, but he is listed as probable for Saturday's game. On the other hand, versatile offensive lineman Ryan Fodje is listed as doubtful for Saturday's game. Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. Establishing the run game will be critical against a Kentucky defense that allowed 240 rushing yards in last Saturday's 34-6 loss at Tennessee. picks.headline: Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh
picks.blurb: Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Story by Wildcats Wire Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Wed, November 11, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Kentucky football failed the first test of this important November stretch, losing 34-6 to Tennessee . The Wildcats have to get off the mat quickly as they host the Florida Gators on Saturday night at Kroger Field. This is a Florida team that is reeling as they have lost four of their last five games. We will preview both sides of the football for the Gators, but we will start with their offense which is led by their star running back. Running back Jadan Baugh is essentially the entire Gators offense, he is the engine that makes it go. Similar to what we said about Tennessee's DeSean Bishop, but the Gators have struggled recently to get this run game going. That is the main reason they have lost four of their last five games. When you look at the win/loss splits of Baugh's stat line, it tells the whole story of Florida's offense. In the Gators' five wins this season, Baugh has rushed for 691 yards on 108 attempts for 12 rushing touchdowns and is averaging over six yards per carry in those wins. He has averaged 138 rushing yards per game in those five wins. Conversely, in Florida's four losses this season, Baugh has rushed for 145 yards on 52 attempts for 2 rushing touchdowns and is averaging under three yards per carry. He is averaging just 36 rushing yards per game in those losses. Teams have started to key in on the run game and slow Baugh down recently, as most of his success came in the first month of the season. In September when the Gators were rolling, Baugh had 600 rushing yards on 83 attempts and 11 of his 14 rushing touchdowns came in the first month of the season. He was averaging 150 rushing yards per game and over seven yards per carry in the month of September. Since then, Baugh has just 236 rushing yards on 77 attempts, averaging just 47 rushing yards per game and three yards per carry. It is simple for Kentucky's defense, stop this rushing attack led by Baugh and you will be in a great position to win this football game. Florida has a quarterback issue, as they have flipped back and forth between Aaron Philo and Tramell Jones. Philo was efficient in the first month of the season, but he dealt with an injury that allowed Jones to start in a big win on the road against Texas. Philo returned against Georgia, but a couple of boneheaded mistakes sent him to the bench. Jones completed 22-of-35 pass attempts for 155 passing yards and two touchdowns with no interceptions in the win over the Longhorns. Against Georgia and Oklahoma, the Gators only scored a total of 15 points. In those two losses, Jones completed 28-of-47 passes for 305 passing yards and no touchdown passes to three interceptions. Jones has thrown just four touchdown passes on the season and five interceptions. Philo on the other hand, has completed 70% of his passes this season for 1,367 yards for nine passing touchdowns. Philo also has five interceptions on the season. The biggest issue has been the injury of wide receiver Vernell Brown, who has not played in a game since the win over Ole Miss in September. Florida is struggling to generate any offense outside of the run game. This matchup is simple for Kentucky, they just have to key in and stop the run game for the Gators. Force Florida into a dropback heavy game, which will lead to turnover opportunities. Regardless if they start Philo or Jones, both have been turnover prone this season and the Gators are -3 in the turnover margin which ranks 98th among FBS teams. Kentucky's defense has to get stops early and play with a lead quickly. This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Florida offense preview: Kentucky has to stop Jadan Baugh

Neither Kentucky nor Florida will feel good coming into this one. Kentucky dropped a stinker in Knoxville, losing 34-6, while Florida got whipped by Oklahoma in The Swamp, 23-7. But they’ll both have to get over it quickly; the SEC comes at you fast. Florida will travel up to Kentucky for a November night game; the last time that happened was just last year. Kentucky rolled to a 38-7 victory. But both coaches are different, and I am not so sure a blowout is in the cards this year for either side. Both teams will look to right the ship and prevent one loss from becoming two. You better believe Jon Sumrall and Brad White will be coming back to Lexington with a win on their minds, while Kentucky will be looking to take the awful sting of that Volunteer loss out of their system while also keeping their College Football Playoff hopes afloat. Florida Gators (5-4, 3-4) Florida is a shockingly inconsistent team. The Gators destroyed Ole Miss by 24, knocked off Texas by 3, but lost by 28 to Missouri and 16 to Oklahoma. The Gators have been held to under 10 points in back-to-back games while also playing a QB carousel. Trammel Jones started against the Sooners but was a dreadful 10-of-22 with 2 INTs. But just a game before, Aaron Philo started 5-of-7, but those two incompletions were interceptions, and he was benched before halftime. Where the Gators go from there is anyone’s guess, but Kentucky will need to prepare to see both guys. On defense, Florida is just as volatile. 425.3 total yards per game is what they give up for the year, but in the last 3 games, they have surrendered 278 yards to Texas, 318 to Georgia, and 351 to Oklahoma. So, Brad White has got his side playing a little better. But it really comes down to which team shows up. Will it be the team that knocked off Texas or the team that lost at home to Oklahoma? ESPN win probability: ESPN FPI gives Kentucky a 54% chance of victory Our prediction I’m not going to lie, this game has got weirdness written all over it. Kentucky and Florida are both coming off terrible losses, with both fan bases hurting. Whichever team handles that the best will walk away with a victory here. I think if Kentucky can get back to playing clean football, they have the talent and home-field advantage to send the Gators back home with a loss. But Florida has a lot of talent, and if they are motivated, they can beat anyone, anywhere, as proven down in Austin when they knocked off Texas. My biggest concern remains Malachi Wood, who has been abused by speed guys this season. Emmanuel Oyebadejo is a 6’6, 300-pound nightmare who leads the Gators with 4.5 sacks. You better believe he is licking his chops to go against the right side of Kentucky’s line, which struggled down in Knoxville. picks.headline: Florida vs. Kentucky predictions, picks, odds: Tuesday's lines for Week 11
picks.blurb: Florida enters the matchup unranked in both major polls with a 5-4 overall record and a 3-4 mark in conference play after its 23-7 loss to Oklahoma at home on Saturday. Kentucky, on the other hand, is 7-2 (5-2 SEC) and ranked 13th in both the US LBM Coaches Poll and AP Top 25 heading into the 11th week of the college football slate, but is also coming off a defeat of their own - a 34-6 beatdown by Tennessee in Knoxville this past weekend. The Gators hold a commanding lead in the all-time series, with a 55-22 record against the Wildcats dating back to 1917, plus a 22-13 mark in Lexington. However, UK won the battle at Kroger Field last year, 38-7, and has prevailed in four of the last five meetings with UF. Just when the defense appeared to be figuring some things out, the offense has mysteriously gone AWOL. Perhaps part of the reason is the absence of Vernell Brown III, who has been out of action since his injury during the Ole Miss game, and also the futility of the running game, which had been among the most formidable in the country over the first four games of the season before evaporating before our eyes. Kentucky's defense has been decent this season, but nowhere near elite, ranking 44th overall in the SP+ ratings and 71st according to Pro Football Focus - which also ranks the run defense at 95th - so Florida's offense could potentially figure things out.
