picks.headline: How No. 11 Kentucky football and Florida match up — with a game prediction
picks.blurb: • Kentucky’s Kenny Minchey (69.9% completions, 1,979 yards, 14 touchdowns vs. two interceptions) had two uncharacteristic turnovers in UK’s disappointing 34-6 loss at Tennessee last Saturday. The 6-2, 211-pound, fourth-year player from Hendersonville, Tennessee, threw his first interception in seven games on a shot play into the end zone. Minchey also lost a fumble after being hit on a UT blitz. • Florida coach Jon Sumrall has not committed to a starting QB this week. Georgia Tech transfer Aaron Philo (70.5% completions, 1,367 yards, nine TDs, five picks) began the season as the UF starter but suffered a shoulder injury on his throwing arm (right) in Florida’s 38-19 loss to South Carolina on October 10. Philo returned in the Gators’ 27-8 loss to Georgia on Halloween, but was ineffective. Tramell Jones Jr . (65.8% completions, 712 yards, four TDs, five interceptions) led UF to its 27-24 road upset of then-No. 7 Texas on Oct. 17 but has thrown no touchdowns and three picks in the two games since. Advantage : Kentucky Running backs • After carrying only once in Kentucky’s two previous games, UK leading rusher CJ Baxter (541 yards, 5.5 yards a carry, eight touchdowns) ran the ball 11 times for 54 yards and caught four passes for 19 yards in the loss at Tennessee. Redshirt senior Jovantae Barnes (272 yards, 5.4 yards a carry, one touchdown in six games) carried seven times for 48 yards at Tennessee but lost a costly fumble. Third-year player Jason Patterson (473 yards, 6.1 yards a carry, three TDs) had 30 yards rushing on seven carries in Knoxville and caught a pass for four yards. • Florida’s Jadan Baugh (836 yards, 5.2 yards a carry, 14 touchdowns) is one of the best backs in college football. However, after the 6-1, 225-pound junior from Atlanta ran for more than 130 yards in each of UF’s first four games, he has run for more than 60 yards only once in the past five contests. As a freshman in 2024, Baugh ran for 106 yards and five touchdowns vs. Kentucky in a 48-20 Gators’ win in Gainesville. Advantage : Florida Wide receivers • Kentucky’s Kenny Darby is tied for the team lead in receptions (45) and leads the Wildcats in receiving yards (576). The 6-1, 180-pound product of Bossier City, Louisiana, caught seven passes for 69 yards in the loss at Tennessee. After missing UK’s win over Vanderbilt due to injury, senior Nic Anderson (20 receptions, 223 yards, one TD) returned at Tennessee and caught three passes for 26 yards. • At 6-3, Florida’s Dallas Wilson (35 catches, 465 yards, three TDs) gives the Gators a big target on the outside. Wilson caught four passes for 48 yards in UF’s 23-7 loss to Oklahoma last week. A transfer from Georgia Tech, Bailey Stockton (36 catches, 373 yards, three touchdowns) provides Florida a steady threat in the slot. • Kentucky’s Willie Rodriguez (45 catches, 405 yards, three touchdowns) has caught multiple passes in all nine UK games to date and has had four receptions or more in seven. The 6-4, 249-pound, third-year player from Covington Catholic High School had one catch for eight yards in last season’s 38-7 Kentucky pummeling of Florida at Kroger Field. Mikkel Skinner (10 catches, 97 yards, one TD), a 6-4, 235-pound second-year player, has carried the ball seven times out of the backfield and caught three passes combined in Kentucky’s past three contests. • Florida’s Luke Harpring , another Gator transfer who followed offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner from Georgia Tech, has made 14 catches for 165 yards. Junior Amir Jackson has made his seven catches count: They have gone for 133 yards and a touchdown. Jackson had a 48-yard catch in UF’s 44-39 win at Auburn on Sept. 19. Offensive line • In the loss at Tennessee, the Kentucky offensive front surrendered four quarterback sacks, six QB hurries and eight tackles for loss. Nevertheless, ESPN analyst Cole Cubelic wrote that UK center Coleton Price , the 6-3, 308-pound transfer from Baylor, “showed up, (and) had a great game.” • Another transfer from Georgia Tech, Florida center Harrison Moore is the interior anchor of the Gators’ front. Left guard Knijeah Harris has started UF’s past 34 games. Defensive line • Kentucky end Mi’Quise Humphrey-Grace (32 tackles, six sacks, nine tackles for loss, nine quarterback hurries) made five stops, 1.5 TFL and had a sack at Tennessee. Tackle Tavion Gadson (29 tackles, three sacks, five TFL, two pass breakups, two fumble recoveres) had four tackles with a TFL vs. UT. • Florida sophomore edge Jayden Woods (37 tackles, 4.5 sacks) is disruptive. End Emmanuel Oyebadejo , a 6-6, 299-pound senior from Manchester, England, had 2.5 sacks in UF’s win at Auburn and has 4.5 on the season. Advantage : Even • Kentucky MLB Grant Godfrey remains second in the SEC in tackles with 78. The 6-3, 240-pound fourth-year player made six stops at Tennessee. Godfrey had three stops, including a tackle for loss in UK’s win over Florida last season. WLB Bo Barnes (60 tackles, 3.5 TFL) made seven stops vs. UT. • Florida WLB Myles Graham , a 6-1, 228-pound, homegrown junior from Gainesville, leads Florida in tackles with 70 and has four sacks, five TFL, three QB hurries and two fumble recoveries. Graham had a season-high 15 tackles in last week’s loss to Oklahoma. MLB Aaron Chiles has made 52 tackles, broken up three passes and recovered a fumble. Defensive backs • Kentucky will start a pair of former Florida Gators in its secondary. Safety Jordan Castell is tied for the SEC lead in interceptions with four and is tied for sixth in the league with 68 tackles. Last year, playing for Florida, Castell made seven tackles vs. UK. Nickelback Aaron Gates , another ex-Gator, is tied for fifth in the SEC with seven passes defended. In last season’s win over Florida, safety Ty Bryant tied for the UK team lead with six. This year, the senior from Frederick Douglass High School is tied for the SEC lead with four picks and has made 68 tackles, broken up three passes and recovered a fumble. • Florida free safety DJ Coleman has made 39 tackles, intercepted two passes and broken up three. Right cornerback Ben Hanks III leads UF with four pass breakups. Even as the Florida secondary has struggled, former Kentucky safety Cam Dooley , who made 29 tackles and picked off a pass last season for UK, has played a minimal role and has made only two tackles so far this season. Special teams • Kentucky place-kicker Adam Zouagui supplied all of UK’s points in the loss at Tennessee with field goals of 43 and 25 yards. On the season, Zouagui is 12 of 15 on field goals with a long make of 52 yards. Punter Wilson Berry averaged 37 yards on three kicks vs. UT, but twice pinned the Volunteers inside their 20-yard line. On the season, the Australian is averaging 42.7 yards and has stopped six of his 13 punts inside the opponents’ 20-yard line. • Florida punter Alec Clark , who formerly kicked for both Marshall and Tulane, is averaging 47.1 yards a kick and has pinned foes inside their 20-yard line on 14 of 31 punts. Place-kicker Patrick Durkin is 11-of-12 on field-goal attempts with a long make of 53 yards. Punt returner Vernell Brown III returned two punts for touchdowns of 64 and 70 yards, respectively, in UF’s 52-3 pasting of Campbell on September 12 but has missed UF’s past five games with a knee injury. home.headline: Final availability report: No. 13 Tennessee vs. No. 6 Kentucky
home.blurb: Head coach Josh Heupel’s team has remained pretty healthy since the early-season injury problems. In this week’s availability reports, the Vols listed no new names and look to have everyone available. Earlier in the week, Heupel was asked how managing a team in November is different than September, and if they are equipped for it. On Friday night’s report , Kentucky reported four players out: inside linebacker Antwan Smith, inside linebacker Justyn Hartley, defensive back Jaden Smith, and defensive back Grant Grayton. Antwan Smith, Jaden Smith, and Grant Grayton have been out for quite some time. Outside linebacker Sam Greene and defensive back Isaiah McMillian were listed as probable. McMillian was initially questionable on Wednesday night but made progress. They are both removed from Saturday's report and available. Xavier Gilliam tunes out the hype as No. 13 Tennessee prepares for No. 6 Kentucky No. 13 Tennessee and No. 6 Kentucky will kick off at 6:20 p.m. ET at Neyland Stadium. The Vols lead the all-time series with 86 wins, 26 losses and 9 ties, and carry a five-game win streak against the Wildcats into Saturday night. “I think you’re constantly trying to improve," Heupel said. "You’ve heard me say it, good teams continue to get better every part of the season. Every week’s its own season, too. And so you’ve got to be great in your preparation, how you practice, put yourself in a position to play smart football. Certainly as you go through the year, injuries, where you’re at, all those things, you have to manage it really week by week. Tends to be more towards the end of the season. But for us this year, we had a bunch of injuries early in the year.” Ninety minutes prior to kickoff, the Southeastern Conference released the final availability report for both teams, which is listed below. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings The Wildcats will try to spoil the Utes' perfect season in a ranked battle Big 12 battle Getty Images Utah's trip to Arizona in Week 11 wasn't circled on many schedules before the 2026 college football season began, but the Big 12 matchup is a showdown between ranked teams and has serious College Football Playoff implications. The Utes are ranked No. 2 in the latest CFP poll as one of two undefeated teams remaining. After beating their hated rivals BYU last week, Utah's path to the Playoff -- and the Big 12 title game -- is clear, but they must turn the page quickly from taking down the Cougars as a trip to Tucson could prove tricky. Arizona climbed to No. 23 in this week's rankings after beating TCU in a thriller, and the 7-2 Wildcats' only losses this season have been to the other top teams in the Big 12 -- BYU and Texas Tech . Both of those losses came on the road, and Arizona will be relishing the opportunity to prove they belong in the top tier of the Big 12 when they finally get to welcome one of the big boys to southern Arizona. For the Utes, a win writes their name into the CFP bracket in pencil, as they'd improve to 10-0 with two games left where they'd be heavy favorites over TCU and West Virginia . The Wildcats, meanwhile, can pick up the biggest win of Brent Brennan's tenure and solidify their place in the Big 12's upper tier. Utah vs. Arizona: Need to know Refocusing the Utes: The Utes put everything they had into winning The Holy War last week against BYU, in the first-ever matchup between the rivals while both were ranked in the top 10. It was obvious how much they put into the game plan with their hot start, and then they were forced to dig deep and rally after the Cougars answered with some haymakers of their own. That win was a proof point for Morgan Scalley in his first season as head coach, but this week might show us more about the kind of culture he's building in Salt Lake City. There's a natural urge to exhale after that kind of win, but Arizona is going to be juiced up for the chance to face the No. 2 team in the country at home. The Utes have to find a way to match that energy -- or at least withstand an early onslaught -- and get the game back on their terms. Strength on strength in the pass game: Arizona is one of the best passing offenses in the country with veteran quarterback Noah Fifita who is both efficient with a 73% completion rate and dynamic with 23 pass plays of 30-plus yards -- third-most in the country. Fifita and his favorite target Isaiah Mizell can take the lid off of most defenses and apply constant stress -- especially with Fifita's ability to extend plays and get outside the pocket. However, they'll be going up against one of the nation's best pass defenses that had Bear Bachmeier completely lost a week ago. Utah is allowing opposing quarterbacks to complete just 51.3% of passes (2nd lowest in the country) and is tied for fourth in interceptions with 13 (including four last week). The Utes pass defense is hyper aggressive, and they have four players with two or more interceptions this season. If there is one weakness to the Utah defense, it is that they have been susceptible to big plays in the passing game. The Utes have allowed 15 pass plays of 30+ yards this season, which ranks 104th in the country. Fifita and Arizona will have to take advantage of those opportunities for chunk plays when they present themselves because moving the ball consistently against the Utes is incredibly difficult. Arizona's pass rush vs. Devon Dampier : The Utes defense will get plenty of attention, but Arizona hasn't been a slouch on that side of the ball this year either. The strength of their defense is their pass rush, which is 10th in the nation in sacks per game (3.11). Devon Dampier is a tough quarterback to wrangle with his combination of strength and elusiveness, but the Wildcats are going to try to heat up Dampier to create some negative plays or, more ideally, turnovers. How Utah's offensive line handles Arizona's rush and how Dampier manages plays when the Wildcats do get pressure on him will be critical in this game. Utah has allowed just 13 sacks this season, thanks to a quality offensive line and Dampier's escapability, but that will be put to the test against the Wildcats. If Arizona is going to win this game, they need to find ways to get the Utes' offense behind the sticks and probably need to win the turnover battle. The pass rush is going to be their best weapon to accomplish both of those goals, and if Arizona is going to pull off the upset, expect the pass rush to be leading the charge. Where to watch Utah vs. Arizona live Date : Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time : 7:30 p.m. ET Location : Casino Del Sol Stadium -- Tucson, Arizona TV: Fox | Live stream: Fubo (try free) Utah vs. Arizona prediction, picks The Wildcats are a good football team and should provide a big test for the Utes coming off last week's win. That said, so far this season, when Arizona has played the best teams in the Big 12, it has proven to be lagging just a bit behind. Over 60 minutes, I expect that to be the case again on Saturday, even with a raucous environment in Tucson for their biggest home game in years. Utah won't have it easy, but when the clock hits triple zeroes, I expect the Utes to move to 10-0 and cover the short number. picks.blurb: Utah vs Arizona Prediction: The Wildcats' Playoff Shot - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Poch leaving for Man U Sportscaster Dan Hicks dies Steph Curry out at least 2 weeks NFL midseason grades Skubal suitors emerge Utah vs Arizona Prediction: The Wildcats' Playoff Shot Pete Fiutak · College Football News Wed, November 11, 2026 at 9:44 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Stuff just got real in a wild Big 12. Utah is No. 2 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings after its win over BYU. Arizona is No. 23 after pulling off a minor miracle to get by TCU, and now the Wildcats get their chance to make a massive splash and jump headfirst in the CFP chase. Getting to the Big 12 Championship isn't out of the question, but losses to BYU and Texas Tech make that hard. However, take down the unbeaten and No. 2 team, and watch the Cats rocket up the rankings. Or , Utah could come up with a terrific ranked win on the road, and at 10-0, it would all but lock up a spot in the CFP. Utah vs Arizona: Quick Hits Arizona still has work to do after this, no matter what, with a trip to Kansas State before hosting the Territorial Cup rivalry game against Arizona State. Utah has a sneaky-tough date at TCU after this before finishing with a sneaky-nasty game against a high-powered West Virginia. Arizona won the last meeting 23-10 in 2024, but Utah is 6-2 in the last eight meetings. How To Watch Utah vs Arizona Date: Saturday, November 11, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: FOX Location: Casino Del Sol Stadium, Tucson, AZ – Week 11 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – How many 3-loss CFP teams will there be? Why Utah Will Win The Utes have been a machine when it comes to controlling the tempo and the time. They're great on third downs on both sides of the ball, the pass defense holds up great when pushed – it'll bend, but doesn't break – and they always seem to have the ball. They can hit the deep shots and be explosive, but they're at their best when quarterback Devon Dampier and the running game go on long marches. Utah keeps the ball a Big 12-best 32:50 a game, but … Why Arizona Will Win Arizona can match the Utes when it comes to tempo. Utah is No. 1 in the conference in time of possession, but Arizona holds the ball for well over 32 minutes, quarterback Noah Fifita is great at hitting short-range third-down throws, and the defense is usually a killer against the run. This isn't necessarily a ball-hawking Wildcat defense, but it's been better at taking the ball away with six over the last four games. Utah has turned it over twice in each ofthe last five games. Utah vs Arizona Prediction, Betting Lines It's all about the Utah ground game and whether or not it will go off. Arizona is 6-0 when allowing fewer than 100 rushing yards, and that includes holding down Cincinnati – the Big 12's No. 2 ground game – and a decent Iowa State attack. Who did the Cats get gouged by? Texas Tech ripped off 320 yards, West Virginia ran for over 300, and BYU averaged close to five yards per carry – the Wildcats lost to the Red Raiders and Cougars. Utah runs well, and it'll get a few gashing runs, but it was held in check by Colorado in Boulder, and didn't run all that well against BYU last week. But here's Utah's biggest problem – the Arizona pass rush. Dampier can move and make plays, but he and the Utah backfield get hit behind the line too often. The other issue for the Utes is a lack of pass rush that should bother Fifita enough to matter in key moments late. Arizona will survive, helped by a +2 turnover margin. picks.blurb: Utah Utes expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm November 13, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football During their decade-plus together in the Pac-12, Arizona and Utah had plenty of great battles, but the results tended to be streaky. The Wildcats won four straight meetings from 2012-15, then Utah took six in a row before the UA claimed the last two, including their Big 12 debut in 2024 when it beat a Top 10 Utes squad on the road. But the opponent coming to Tucson this weekend is better than any of those previous versions. Utah is 9-0 and ranked No. 2 nationally, one of two unbeaten teams in FBS. To better understand the Utes, we reached out to Josh Furlong of KSL.com for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his spirited answers to our lifeless questions: AZ Desert Swarm: What have been the main keys to Utah getting off to its best start since 2008? Josh Furlong: “The easy answer is quarterback Devon Dampier, who has been healthy and efficient as the team’s biggest playmaker, but it ultimately comes down to the culture Morgan Scalley has built at Utah in such a short time. He’s allowing the players to be loose while focused, understanding that it takes each person to contribute to wins. He’s an extremely competitive coach, but he’s able to pair that with a system that allows players to make mistakes, grow and develop.” Arizona fans still have nightmares about Devon Dampier from two years ago at New Mexico, and he seems to have only gotten better. Where has his game most improved this season, and is there anything he still struggles with? “Dampier has worked on going through his progressions and staying in the pocket more, which has allowed Utah to do more with him at QB. It’s giving him more structure while understanding that he still needs room to freelance and be the dynamic QB he can be. All of that has allowed him to have more confidence, especially now that he’s been paired with a better group of wide receivers. At times, though, he gets happy feet and doesn’t have the right mechanics in his throws, which can sometimes limit his passing.” Wayshawn Parker apparently got banged up against BYU but should be good to go for this game. What does he bring to the offense when healthy? “Wayshawn Parker simply opens up the options for Utah’s offense. His threat as a runner, especially as he breaks through tackles, makes him one of the top offensive names you have to take away. But by doing so, opposing defenses have to handle many other players that can be just as effective in advancing the offense — Dampier, Daniel Bray, Byrd Ficklin, Braden Pegan, Creed Whittemore, etc. On top of that, he’s really developed a great pass blocking game, which has been a huge advantage in keeping Dampier upright and doing what he does.” Arizona’s secondary has been dealing with injuries and got exploited a bit last week with deep passes. Who would be the beneficiaries of this in the Ute receiving corps? “The primary receiving target would be Braden Pegan (WR1), who is a multi-faceted receiver who can do pretty much anything needed, and is paired with Ricky Johnson and Creed Whittemore. Johnson is a smooth runner with great separation and great hands. Whittemore works primarily in the slot and has been great in the intermediate game, especially with opposing defenses focusing on Pegan and the potential run threats of Dampier, Ficklin, Parker. Another option is tight end Noah Bennee, who is the benefactor of all the other skills players being the top of mind. As the defense focuses on other players, Bennee sneaks out and can be a problem with his size.” How do you expect Utah to defend Arizona’s passing attack? “Utah will primarily operate in man coverage and force Noah Fifita to beat them one-on-one, while the defensive coordinator Colton Swan schemes up disguises and blitzes to keep Fifita uncomfortable. Because Fifita is so explosive, it’s likely Utah will try more contain while pressuring him.” Morgan Scalley had been the coach in waiting at Utah for a while, and we’re seeing why with this 9-0 start. What are the biggest differences between him and Kyle Whittingham? “The biggest difference is that Scalley is a people’s person. Kyle Whittingham cared more about coaching football and not the other elements, whereas Scalley sees it all interconnected. He shares the same hard-nosed, physical approach of Whittingham but wants a connected team that has no factions. It’s not, offense gets to know offense and defense gets to know defense, it’s a team-wide look as each works to understand the other. He’s also open to feedback, assuming that the feedback actually is presented in a way that helps change and it’s just complaining, though he’d listen to anyone who is frustrated. He wants all to feel connected and bought into the program, regardless of their standing with the team.” Prediction time. Does Utah move one step closer to an unbeaten regular season or does Arizona pull off a November upset at home and stay in the hunt for the Big 12 title game and the playoffs? Give us a score pick. “This game in Tucson is always a tricky one. Even when Utah has been the clear favorite, it’s far from a decisive win for the Utes. I think Scalley has his squad more focused on this game than it might have been in year’s past, which leads me to believe Utah will be ready for any blow and not be caught off guard in a road environment. I think Utah is the more complete team, but they’ve got to stop Fifita. To me, Utah wins this game if they can contain Fifita (as much as possible) and cannot give up momentum to an opposing crowd. I see Utah winning something like 31-24 .” Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. picks.blurb: Arizona Wildcats football vs. Utah Utes score predictions | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm November 13, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football Twice this season, Arizona has found itself up against a ranked opponent with a chance to make a big splash on the national stage, and both times it led at halftime only to fall in the end. Third time’s a charm? No. 22 Arizona (7-2, 4-2) plays its biggest game of the year on Saturday, hosting unbeaten No. 2 Utah (9-0, 6-0) with a chance to climb back into the Big 12 title race and the hunt for a College Football Playoff spot. How will the Wildcats do in this Top 25 clash? Our staff makes its predictions. Kim Doss — Utah wins 30-28 Utah is not a team that has difficulty scoring. The Utes average 34.3 points per game against their FBS opponents this season. Their lowest output was 21 points against Houston. They’ve only been held below 30 points by three of their FBS opponents: Houston, BYU, and (surprisingly) Colorado. Arizona will be Utah’s third ranked opponent but first on the road. Will it matter that the game isn’t in Salt Lake City? Doubtful. The Wildcats had issues with mobile quarterbacks. While Arizona is ranked fifth in the Big 12 with 203.3 pashing yards allowed per game, Devon Dampier doesn’t just rely on his arm to move the ball. He throws for 228.1 ypg. He’s also second on the team in rushing with 53.6 ypg on the ground. Dampier is going to be playing in his home state against his former head coach. The now-assistant coach at Arizona admits that he should have played Dampier more when they were both at New Mexico. The senior from Phoenix may have something to prove and a group of friends and family members in attendance to prove it to. On the positive side, Arizona should be able to move the ball, too. Utah is ninth in the Big 12 in passing yards allowed at 233.8 per game. Noah Fifita is fourth in the nation in passing yards per game (310.4), total passing yards (2,794), and total offense per game (325.4). The Arizona defense has been solid for most of the year, but it barely kept the Big 12’s 15 th -ranked scoring offense under 30 points last week. Utah is the No. 2 scoring offense in the league. The Wildcats are No. 6. To make matters worse for the ‘Cats, Utah has the No. 2 scoring defense in the Big 12. Arizona’s in No. 5. With some luck, this one could be close. It would be a shocker to see Arizona pull off the upset, though. Ezra Amacher — Utah wins 27-24 Utah’s Devon Dampier is the type of quarterback that gives Arizona defensive coordinator Danny Gonzales cold sweats at night. The senior from Saguaro High School in Phoenix has grown into one of top dual-threat quarterbacks in the country. He ranks second among all active FBS quarterbacks with 2,811 career rushing yards. He has a dang good arm as well and doesn’t commit many turnovers. Arizona struggled to stop the other dual-threat QBs it faced this year in TCU’s Jaden Craig and West Virginia’s Michael Hawkins Jr. Dampier is better than either of them and has a stalwart offensive line protecting him. I don’t see the Wildcats defense being able to do enough to keep Utah off the board. That wouldn’t be as much of a concern against a lesser opponent, but Utah’s defense is outstanding. The Utes give up 16.3 points per game, second-fewest in the Big 12. They’re riding high on confidence after forcing BYU’s Bear Bachmeier into four interceptions last week. I give Utah the edge. Adam Green — Arizona wins 31 -27 Why the hell not. Here in this space is where I try to convince you all (and myself, really) that this pick is an actual prediction rather than wischasting. So here we go. Arizona is good — very good — at home. Utah has not beaten a ranked team on the road. Arizona has everything to play for and is coming off a victory that likely served as a wake up call while inspiring confidence. Utah, on the other hand, has a little bit of breathing room and is coming off an emotional and physical victory over rival BYU. Finally, Arizona has Noah Fifita . The QB is a perfect 2-0 against Morgan Scalley’s defense, with the most recent victory coming in Salt Lake City during a season in which the Wildcats were not a particularly good team. That Fifita is playing the best football of his career heading into this game and has weapons like Isaiah Mizell and Giovanni Richardson is nothing to feel bad about. This isn’t to say that it will be an easy game like the last time these teams played in Tucson, because it’s hard to imagine No. 2 in the nation going down without a fight. Utah’s offense is going to be more dynamic than we’re used to seeing but their defense is gettable for an Arizona team that is quite capable of slinging the ball around. Keep penalties to a minimum and win the turnover battle, and Arizona will win the game. Juan Serrano — Arizona wins 31-28 Arizona is a different team when it plays inside Casino Del Sol Stadium. Of course, last week’s game was a miracle and not usually how the Wildcats play at home. The defense did only surrendered 21 points to TCU which is usually a winning formula. Noah Fifita ’s pick-six was a rarity and kept the Horned Frogs in the game. He cannot afford to have those type of plays against Utah, and I don’t think he will. Fifita usually has some of his best games against the Utes. I also think Arizona missed two shots at a big win against BYU and Texas Tech. It’s time for the ball to bounce in the way of the Wildcats in terms of making a statement. Utah has only been favored by 2.5 since the end of the Holy War, and it has stuck there. That is a very good sign for Arizona. Devon Dampier does present a big issue for the defense but I would not be surprised if Danny Gonzales presents a different picture for Dampier. He knows his defense has struggled against mobile quarterbacks and it has shown in many games. Something will need to change schematically for the Wildcats to have a chance to win. It all comes down to what is at stake for Arizona. This is a season defining, program defining moment for Brent Brennan ’s squad. The home winning streak will continue for the Wildcats and will earn one of the most historic wins in Arizona football history. Brandon Combs — Arizona wins 30-24 I’m not going to lie, I’ve been tossing this one back and forth in my mind. The Wildcats at home are a force to be reckoned with. I throw out the issues from Arizona last week as kind of fluky. They were coming off an emotional loss against Texas Tech, and on a short week no less. Noah Fifita’s rare and odd pick six, Dwight Bootle’s rough night and the not-great tackling were all things that caused the closeness of the game against TCU. On the other side, you have Utah coming off an physical and emotional Holy War win against BYU last week. As of this writing, Utah looks like they’ll be without their leader in sacks, DL Karson Kaufusi , who has 3 sacks this year. However, the Utes still have Jireh Moe and Elijah Elliss , who are also fantastic d-linemen and have combined for 62 tackles, 9.5 TFLs and 5 sacks. Overall, this game is going to come down to QB play. Not breaking any news here, but Noah is a stud and will have to play a near flawless game. If he plays his game and doesn’t force anything, or make any plays like last week’s pick six, Arizona has a legit chance to win. For the Utes, Devon Dampier is a problem. He has been effective through the air this season, however, his legs are his biggest strength. He is a fantastic runner and is Utah’s second leading rusher. Even if he doesn’t gain massive yards, he is able to extend plays and forces the defense to respect his running ability. Finally, I think Danny Gonzales will change some things up for Utah. I don’t expect to see the same looks that TCU got, mainly due to the injuries on defense. I believe Danny has learned from the Tommy Castellanos issues and won’t make it as easy for Dampier. Couple that with slowing down Wayshawn Parker and playing in front of what seems to be turning into a packed Sol, I think the defense can do it. Brian Pedersen — Arizona wins 21-20 As I wrote earlier this week , November has traditionally been the month when Arizona has picked up its biggest home wins. It’s been a while, though, and most of those have been when the Wildcats are a decided underdog and the game isn’t in the national spotlight. Not the case this time, with a very small spread and Fox’s Big Noon Kickoff is in town. The losses at BYU and Texas Tech had a common theme beyond leading at halftime. Both saw the UA struggle mightily in the second half, scoring only nine total points, though each time it was down four and driving with a chance to go back in front. One missed play turned everything. Utah is a very good team with no weakness, and has the kind of dual-threat weapon in Devon Dampier that Arizona traditionally struggles with. But it’s November, and strange things happen at night in the desert. The Longhorns have recovered from a few early miscues and jumped back into the SEC title race. The Longhorns have won three straight games, including a 34-20 win over No. 18 Missouri last week. LSU faced its biggest test of the season against No. 5 Alabama and faltered, losing 31-13. The Tigers were unable to find any offensive consistency in the loss, rushing for only 2.3 yards per carry as the Crimson Tide won in all three phases. Texas and LSU have only played 18 times in history, and not in Baton Rouge since 1953. The last time they played was in 2019, when legendary quarterback Joe Burrow threw a dramatic touchdown pass on third-and-17 to put the game away. Texas vs. LSU: Need to know Arch settling down: Texas quarterback Arch Manning had some growing pains midseason, especially with inconsistent performances against Florida and Oklahoma . But over the last two weeks, the former No. 1 overall recruit has come into his own. The junior is completing 76% of his passes with six touchdowns and zero interceptions over the last two wins. Top defenses: Statistically, Texas and LSU are two of the top three defenses in the SEC, joining Georgia in nearly every relevant category. The Tigers are better against the run, holding opponents to 2.7 yards per carry. Texas is especially good against the pass, holding opponents to 5.4 yards per pass attempt with eight touchdowns to six interceptions. Expect a low-scoring battle in Death Valley. Major CFP implications: Texas remains in solid shape for the postseason, even with a third loss, because of their strong resume. LSU, though? The Tigers' dreams are almost completely dead. They are 0-3 against ranked opponents and ranked outside of the top 20 in the CFP Rankings. picks.headline: Brian Kelly Makes Bold Prediction for LSU-Texas Week 11 Showdown
picks.blurb: Brian Kelly Makes Bold Prediction for LSU-Texas Week 11 Showdown Skip to main content SI.COM TRANSFER PORTAL More from CFB-HQ On SI NEWS A pair of SEC blue blood contenders face off under the lights, each playing in seemingly different directions, and with serious postseason implications for both. LSU has split its last two games, is coming off an ugly loss to Alabama, and is outside the playoff bubble. Texas is on a three-game win streak, has defeated two ranked SEC opponents, and is the No. 6 team in the bracket. Looking at the matchup, Brian Kelly sees this going one way, and for one reason. Brian Kelly projects LSU-Texas matchup “I think in this game, one can be fixed and the other can’t. And that is, I don’t know if Texas can protect. I don’t think you can fix that over a week,” Kelly said on CBS Sports. "I don't know if Texas can protect. I don't think you can fix that over a week." @CoachBrianKelly is going with @LSUFootball over the Horns this weekend 👀 pic.twitter.com/9fap1Zx4aH “For LSU, it’s situational football. They have to be better in the red zone. They have to be better in fourth down situations. I think you can correct situational football with execution. I don’t know if [the Longhorns] can protect. I’m going with LSU.” Longhorns have struggled at the line Winning games and getting better play from Arch Manning has lifted much of the negative attention around Texas at a critical point of the season. But what happens in the trenches could decide who prevails in Death Valley, and on paper that matchup may not go the Longhorns’ way. Coming into this weekend, Texas has allowed 27 sacks of Manning. That number accounts for the ninth-most of any team in college football this year. Moreover, issues with blocking have conspired against their rushing offense. McElroy pointed to the quarterback’s patience as part of the problem. “He does hold the ball looking for the perfect throw, and behind that line, the perfect throw sometimes arrives after the defense arrives,” McElroy said. Edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, an Austin native who followed Kiffin from Ole Miss, is the player McElroy expects to attack a Texas line that has struggled with twists and stunts. LSU and Texas are set to meet in Baton Rouge this weekend in a matchup that could officially eliminate the Tigers from the College Football Playoff conversation. With three losses, LSU's playoff hopes are already on life support. A fourth loss would pull the plug. Texas, meanwhile, needs to win to avoid a third loss, which would put their playoff chances in jeopardy. ESPN's Greg McElroy predicts the final score of Texas vs LSU ESPN's Greg McElroy made his picks for this weekend's biggest college football games, and he has LSU winning a close one over Texas. LSU has a 25% chance to make the College Football Playoff and a 3% chance to win the national title, according to the A to Z Sports CFB Playoff Predictor (updated November 8, 2026). "LSU runs more plays than anyone in the entire FBS — nearly 80 a game — and at a pace that doesn't let Texas substitute," said McElroy . "Texas is used to facing about 68 plays by the opposing offense. So, if LSU's tempo has the Texas linebackers gasped by the fourth quarter, and the best defense on the field stops being the best defense on the field, then [it's a positive for the Tigers]. "LSU's pass rush against Texas's protection is probably the most lopsided matchup on the board. It's happening at home at night. The Texas defense is good enough to hold LSU to field goals, which is why I think this stays a fight. But if Texas becomes one-dimensional, then an offense that has to throw against this (LSU) pass rush is going to spend way too much time off schedule behind the chains. I'm taking LSU to win this game 24-20 . At night in Death Valley, that's when that pass rush gets a sixth man, and I don't know if Texas's O-line can hold up throughout the night." The Longhorns are 7-2 and No. 6 in the latest College Football Playoff rankings. The Tigers are 6-3 and all the way down at No. 21. If Texas wins … boom. It will have eight victories, including great wins over Ohio State, Tennessee, Ole Miss, and Missouri, to go along with two 27-24 losses to Florida and Oklahoma. Add a win at LSU to the résumé, and it keeps moving along, but losing one of its last two games to Arkansas or Texas A&M would make it a fight to get in, even with the great résumé of wins. If Texas wins, LSU is done. However, even at 6-3, things might get a bit interesting if LSU pulls this off. The three losses to No. 3 Alabama, No. 11 Kentucky, and No. 19 Ole Miss might end the debate, except for one key factor – next week, the Tigers play at No. 8 Tennessee. Close strong, hope for a slew of losses from other SEC teams, and … It's Texas at LSU. It should be a great game. Texas vs LSU: Quick Hits Texas still has to face Arkansas next before finishing up the season at Texas A&M – beating the Longhorns would be a season-maker for the Aggies. This is Senior Day for LSU. It's actually a positive that the next game is at Tennessee before finishing up the regular season at Arkansas. The two programs have only played 16 times. LSU won the last meeting 45-38 in 2019, Texas won the 2003 Cotton Bowl, and before that, the last meeting was a 13-0 LSU win in the 1963 Cotton Bowl. How To Watch Texas vs LSU Date: Saturday, November 14, 2026 Game Time: 7:30 PM ET TV: ABC Location: Tiger Stadium, Baton Rouge, LA – Week 11 Schedule, Predictions – CFN Bowl & CFP Projections | Top 25 – How many 3-loss CFP teams will there be? Why Texas Will Win Don't let LSU get into a groove. The offense is fantastic when it finds its rhythm, and moving the ball hasn't been too much of a problem in losses, compared to most normal teams, but if you can keep the Tiger ground game under wraps, everything else tends to be off. LSU threw for 380 yards against Alabama – it had to after getting down – but it only averaged 2.3 yards per carry. The Tigers were stuffed by the Mississippi State run defense, but that wasn't an issue because of the punchless Kamario Taylor-less Bulldog offense. And, not a shocker, the other bad day on the ground for LSU was in the loss to Kentucky, averaging just 2.6 yards per carry. Texas is 16th in the nation against the run, allowing just 2.9 yards per carry. Why LSU Will Win Complete your passes against Texas. The Longhorn defense might be a killer against the run, but it'll give up big plays here and there. It'll be tempting to keep cranking out the deep shots, but LSU's uptempo offense should be able to maintain some semblance of control. Sam Leavitt hasn't always been perfect, but again with the rhythm, he and the LSU attack can be devastating when the passing game clicks. Leavitt is hitting 71% of his throws this year, and even with the team's problems overall against Alabama, he has settled into his role. He hasn't been under 71% since the loss to Ole Miss back in mid-September. Texas vs LSU Prediction, Betting Lines It's a narrative I've seen coming for months. I can't shake it, and I can't back off now. Texas becomes the cause célèbre for the SEC "this three-loss team deserves to be in" faction of the college football world. It has too many good wins; the losses will be close, and dropping a tight battle in Death Valley in a Saturday night fight will be considered as acceptable as it gets. Arch Manning will have deep threat Cam Coleman to open things up, but LSU will bounce back after the problems against Alabama with its first really, really good win. And no, it won't be enough to get LSU back into the College Football Playoff discussion, but it'll be the first giant moment to set the tone for the Lane Kiffin era going forward. away.headline: Texas's initial injury report provided sweet relief ahead of Longhorns' trip to LSU
away.blurb: While defensive tackle Hero Kanu was listed as questionable after suffering a shoulder injury in Texas's Week 10 win over the Missouri Tigers, many of the Horns' previously questionable players were already off the first availability report of the week: OUT: Hollywood Smothers (RB), Trevor Goosby (OL), Nick Townsend (TE), Richard Wesley (EDGE) Meanwhile, the Tigers' first availability report for Week 11 also didn't include quite as many stars for LSU, other than the fact that star linebacker Whit Weeks was listed as "questionable" and not definitively out: OUT: Dashawn Spears (S), Phillip Wright III (WR), Charles Ross II (LB), Richard Anderson (DT) PROBABLE: Gabriel Reliford (DE), Weston Davis (OT) The return of Weeks could spell trouble for Texas's already-shaky offensive line, and the absence of defensive tackle Richard Anderson and linebacker Charles Ross II doesn't exactly provide much reprieve, with neither seeing significant playing time throughout the season so far. In other words, both teams would be pretty close to full strength, or at least as close as possible with a couple of players out for the season. So, no matter which team wins, the other wouldn't be able to point to injuries as the reason for its loss. Over the last few weeks, the Texas Longhorns have seen some of their key players go down in games and subsequently pop up on the team's availability reports . That has included stars like edge rusher Colin Simmons, wide receivers Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo, and defensive back Graceson Littleton. Well, as the Horns' Week 11 matchup against the LSU Tigers has come into focus, Texas was luckily able to remove quite a few of those crucial players from its injury list. In fact, when Steve Sarkisian and the Horns released their initial availability report on Wednesday evening, it included some of the best news possible ahead of the top-25 SEC game. Texas Longhorns' Week 11 initial availability report vs. LSU Tigers Simmons, Coleman, Wingo, Littleton, Kade Phillips, and other stars (on both sides of the ball) were finally off the injury list from the jump, a great sign of the Horns' ability to rehabilitate their players to full health. Of course, the recurring presence of running back Hollywood Smothers and offensive tackle Trevor Goosby should come as no surprise, with both suffering season-ending knee injuries in the last month. Similarly, wideout Phillip Wright III hasn't seen the field since the Tigers' second game of the season. away.headline: LSU injury report: Gabe Reliford probable vs. Texas in return from ACL tear
away.blurb: LSU football defensive end Gabe Reliford was listed as probable for the Texas game on LSU's Wednesday injury report. If Reliford plays, it would be a quick, impressive return from an ACL tear suffered in spring practice. Reliford is yet to suit up in 2026. LSU's defensive end duo of Princewill Umanmielen and Jordan Ross is one of the best in the SEC. Still, Reliford's return would be welcomed, as he provides a physical, bruising presence against the run. With Reliford out, Dylan Carptenger emerged as LSU's core third defensive end and has given Blake Baker's defense valuable reps. Even if Reliford does go, it remains to be seen how he'd factor into the rotation. He's a capable player, but this would be a big spot to return to given how much time he's missed. Anything LSU can get from the third-year defensive end is a positive, though, given it looked like he would miss the entire year after the injury occurred in the spring. LSU's entire defense has been impacted by the injury bug this year. Safety Da'Shawn Spears tore his ACL vs. Ole Miss and is out for the year. Linebacker Whit Weeks has been out since Week 4. This article originally appeared on LSU Wire: LSU injury report: Gabe Reliford probable vs. Texas in return from ACL tear Reliford's spring injury dealt a significant blow to LSU's defensive end depth. Reliford is a talented player who saw immediate playing time as a true freshman in 2024. In 2025, he started strong until shoulder surgery ended his year after four games. The last time Reliford saw the field was LSU's Week 4 win over SE Louisiana in 2025. Prior to the injury, Reliford had four pressures and seven stops. home.headline: Whit Weeks upgraded as LSU gets positive injury report
home.blurb: Linebacker Whit Weeks has been upgraded to questionable as he continues working his way back from a broken fibula. Weeks has been sidelined since LSU’s September 27th win over Texas A&M. He was listed as doubtful on last week’s availability report. There is no doubt Weeks wants to get back to the football field, but there is an added motivation for this Saturday as it Senior Day and it could be his last game in Tiger Stadium, if he chooses not to return for a fifth season. There’s also good news along the offensive line. Starting right tackle Weston Davis is listed as probable after leaving last week’s game on crutches. Davis will be important against a Texas defense led by one of the nation’s top pass rushers, Colin Simmons, who has recorded 10.5 sacks this season. When Davis left the Alabama game, he was replaced by Baylor transfer Sean Thompkins Jr, who graded out poorly according to Pro Football Focus. LSU could also get a boost on the defensive front. Defensive end Gabriel Reliford is listed as probable , which is surprising to see. The former Evangel standout tore his ACL in March and apparently has made a speedy recovery. For Texas, defensive tackle Hero Kanu is listed as questionable after reportedly suffering a torn biceps in last week’s win over Missouri. However, he is expected to try to play through the injury. The first SEC Availability Report of the week brings some encouraging news for LSU ahead of Saturday’s matchup against eighth-ranked Texas. LSU coverage brought to you by Rouses Markets www.audacy.com He also missed most of last season with a torn rotator cuff, but the former four-star prospect played a lot in his freshman season and could be an important piece looking ahead to next year’s team. Texas also appears to have starting receiver Cam Coleman back. Coleman, who missed the Missouri game with a shoulder injury, is not listed on the availability report, indicating he is expected to play Saturday. Coleman has 23 catches for 409 yards and a team-high seven touchdowns this season.

Staff photo by Michael Johnson LSU football lost one of its starting offensive linemen to a leg injury vs. Alabama By REED DARCEY | Staff writer Reed Darcey Nov 7, 2026 Updated Nov 7, 2026 LSU right tackle Weston Davis was injured on Saturday in the third quarter of the Tigers’ 31-13 loss to Alabama. Davis, a redshirt sophomore, left the game after tight end Trey’Dez Green fell at his feet. The two-year starter couldn’t put any weight on his right leg as he was helped off the field and into the medical tent. He then hobbled to the locker room on crutches. LSU inserted Baylor transfer Sean Thompkins in Davis’ place at right tackle. Davis is a former four-star recruit who landed LSU’s starting right tackle job prior to the 2025 season. He and center Braelin Moore are the only holdover starters on the offensive line. Through eight games in 2026, Davis had allowed 21 pressures, according to Pro Football Focus data. Only two Southeastern Conference offensive linemen had surrendered more. In 2025, Davis gave up 33 pressures, which was tied for the third-most in the SEC. home.headline: Whit Weeks and another injured LSU defender could return for Texas game, according to SEC report
home.blurb: Whit Weeks and another injured LSU defender could return for Texas game, according to SEC report By JON BLAU | Staff writer Jon Blau Weeks was categorized as “questionable” for the Tigers’ game against Texas in the Southeastern Conference’s initial release for the week. The senior defender has been sidelined since he suffered a lower-leg injury against Texas A&M on Sept. 26. Weeks was listed as “doubtful” on multiple SEC availability reports in the days leading up to last week’s game against Alabama. The senior was inevitably ruled out the Friday night before a 31-13 loss. LSU could also return another injured defender this Saturday, because defensive end Gabriel Reliford, who suffered an ACL tear in March during spring practice, was listed as probable for the Texas game. LSU coach Lane Kiffin previously said it was unlikely Reliford would return to play this season. Right tackle Weston Davis, who was knocked out by an injury versus Alabama, was also listed as probable for Texas. A listing of “questionable” is supposed to confer that an athlete has about a 50% chance of suiting up for that week’s game. “Doubtful” means closer to a 25% chance — and an “out” designation means a player has been ruled out completely. Aside from Weeks, LSU is without safety Dashawn Spears, receiver Phillip Wright and linebacker Charles Ross, who have all suffered season-ending injuries. But the Tigers remain relatively healthy otherwise, especially since tight end Trey’Dez Green’s return. Freshman defensive tackle Richard Anderson, who missed the Auburn and Alabama contests, was also listed as out on Wednesday’s report.
